Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Questions WBO Over Voluntary Defense Reversal
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is challenging Gustavo Olivieri to explain what changed after claiming the WBO president publicly agreed to let him make a voluntary defense before facing mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez next year.

Bentley’s response follows Olivieri’s explanation that the organization never received a formal petition to approve the proposed fight against Shane Mosley Jr. The dispute leaves two different accounts of how Bentley’s planned voluntary defense reached this point.

“Whether I had an opponent or not this guy agreed and tweeted I get a voluntary defence before the end of the year then fight yo-yo next year which I was happy to do so the question everyone needs to ask is what changed,” Bentley wrote on X.

That is the question Bentley wants answered. His argument is that Olivieri had already accepted the sequence: a voluntary before the end of 2026, followed by Hernandez in 2027.

Olivieri, speaking to Tru School Sports, described a process that still required formal approval.

“We never received a formal petition. From Zuffa, from team Bentley, or from team Mosley for this particular fight.”

The WBO president added that every championship defense requires the approval of its championship committee, whether the opponent is a mandatory challenger or a voluntary selection.

According to Olivieri, Bentley had no date, opponent, or venue when the mandatory obligation needed to be addressed. Hernandez had been the designated challenger since July, and his team submitted a petition seeking enforcement.

Bentley is scheduled to face Mosley on November 7 in London, but the WBO rejected his appeal to take a voluntary defense and instructed him to commit to Hernandez. sports.yahoo.com

The wording of Olivieri’s earlier post is therefore crucial. An explicit agreement allowing Bentley to fight a voluntary before Hernandez would give the British fighter a reasonable basis to question the subsequent ruling. Permission dependent on committee approval would leave Bentley’s team responsible for completing that process.

A public conversation with the president and formal authorization from the championship committee may be separate steps. Bentley’s latest response does not explain whether his team submitted the details needed to secure that authorization.

Hernandez has his own interests to protect. He pursued his mandatory opportunity and asked the WBO to enforce it. Accepting Bentley’s preferred timetable would require him to wait while the champion takes another fight.

Bentley says he was willing to face Hernandez next year. The disagreement is over whether he had permission to take another opponent first—and whether Olivieri’s earlier words support the permission Bentley believes he received.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Falls Short Against Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton “Thunder” Smith (20-0, 14 KOs) retained his WBC light welterweight title with a split decision over former champion Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-2, 11 KOs) on Saturday at a sold-out Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England.

Two judges scored the fight 115-113 for Smith, while the third had Puello ahead 115-112. Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Boxing promoted the event, which aired on DAZN.

The opening six rounds were closely contested, with this writer’s unofficial card even after Puello took the fifth and sixth.

Smith responded well in the seventh and eighth, edging the action as swelling appeared beneath Puello’s left eye. Puello answered with stronger work in the ninth and tenth before Smith took the 11th.

In the final round, a left hand from Puello opened a small cut on Smith’s right cheek. Smith began celebrating during the final 30 seconds, although the divided scorecards showed how close the contest had been.

Lee Every refereed.

Giorgio Visioli Edges Maxi Hughes

Unbeaten southpaw Giorgio “The Italian Job” Visioli (12-0, 6 KOs) defeated veteran Maxi “Maximus” Hughes (29-10-2, 6 KOs) by majority decision over ten rounds to win the vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title.

Two judges scored it 96-94 for Visioli, with the third returning a 95-95 draw.

Visioli’s effective jab helped him through much of the first seven rounds. Hughes opened a cut over Visioli’s left eyebrow with a right jab in the eighth, but Visioli responded and finished strongly enough to secure the decision. Kieran McCann refereed.

Shannon Ryan Stops Emma Dolan In Rematch

Shannon “Kaos” Ryan (12-1, 3 KOs) avenged her previous defeat to Emma Dolan (9-2, 1 KO) with a first-round stoppage in their scheduled ten-round super flyweight rematch.

Around 20 seconds into the fight, Ryan dropped Dolan with a right hand to the side of the face. Dolan rose, but another right followed by a left sent her down again.

Referee Howard Foster stopped the contest at 40 seconds after Dolan regained her feet.

Edward Hardy Outpoints Diego Ruiz

Edward Hardy (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with an eight-round points victory over Diego “El Profeta” Ruiz (28-16-1, 14 KOs).

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-73 for Hardy, who controlled most of the action from the second round onward.

Both fighters maintained a high work rate during an active final round, but Hardy finished with a clear points win.

Joe Hayden Defeats Will Harrison

Joe Hayden (25-0, 4 KOs) handed Will “The Thrill” Harrison (8-1-2, 0 KOs) his first professional defeat in their eight-round welterweight bout.

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-72 for Hayden.

Leo Atang Scores Three Knockdowns In First-Round Stoppage

Nineteen-year-old heavyweight Leo Atang (9-0, 8 KOs) dropped Jonathan “Chicito” Vergara (9-5, 5 KOs) three times before stopping him in the opening round of their scheduled six-round contest.

A right hand dropped Vergara within the first minute. Atang scored another knockdown with a right to the side of the head with approximately 30 seconds remaining.

A third right hand sent Vergara down again in the closing seconds. Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick waved off the fight after Vergara rose, just before the bell.

Chris Mulunda Shuts Out Harley Collison

Chris “Mulla” Mulunda (5-0, 0 KOs) defeated Harley Collison (3-9-2, 0 KOs) by points over six rounds.

Referee Michael Alexander scored every round for Mulunda, returning a 60-54 verdict.

Divine Omojor Wins Professional Debut

Cruiserweight Divine Omojor (1-0, 1 KO) began his professional career with a second-round stoppage of Goran Kozul (8-13, 2 KOs).

Referee Michael Alexander stopped the scheduled four-round bout at 1:52 of the second.

David Diamante served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Emanuel ‘Vaquero’ Navarrete Loses to O’Shaquie ‘Ice Water’ Foster!
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster defeated Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, adding the WBO and IBF super featherweight titles to his WBC championship.

Foster scored two knockdowns in the final round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111. The Top Rank event aired on DAZN.

Foster improved to 26-3 with 12 knockouts, while Navarrete fell to 40-3-1 with 33 knockouts.

Navarrete spent the opening round following Foster without consistently cutting off the ring, allowing Foster to land counters and move away. The second round became scrappier, with Foster tying Navarrete up when he closed the distance.

Navarrete had success with pressure in the third, but Foster’s movement and counterpunching helped him control much of the action over the following rounds. Foster hurt Navarrete during the seventh, forcing him to hold.

Both landed well in the tenth, with Navarrete producing some of his better offensive work. Navarrete also hurt Foster with a heavy shot late in the 11th, giving him encouragement entering the final round.

Foster responded with two knockdowns in the 12th. A counter right sent Navarrete to one knee, and referee Mark Nelson administered the count. Another counter right dropped Navarrete again in the final minute.

Navarrete rose both times and reached the bell, but Foster’s strong finish secured the victory.

Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez

NABF featherweight champion Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts by stopping Edward “Kid” Vazquez at 1:04 of the second round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Vazquez, of Fort Worth, Texas, fell to 20-4 with six knockouts.

Gonzalez overwhelmed Vazquez with a prolonged attack in the second round, then followed him to another corner. Heavy punches to the body sent Vazquez to one knee, where referee Laurence Cole counted him out.

Frank Martin Stops Tarik Zaina

Southpaw Frank “The Ghost” Martin stopped Tarik “El Camello” Zaina at 2:38 of the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title.

Martin improved to 20-1-1 with 14 knockouts, while Zaina dropped to 18-4-1 with 12 knockouts.

Martin had success early, but Zaina’s lead right hands helped keep the middle rounds competitive.

In the final minute of the seventh, Martin landed a combination beginning with a left to the chin that dropped Zaina. Zaina beat referee Angel Mendez’s count, but Martin immediately followed with a flurry that forced Mendez to stop the fight.

Deric Davis Shuts Out Joaquin Silva Faccio

Deric “Scooter” Davis defeated Joaquin Silva Faccio by unanimous decision in their eight-round lightweight bout, winning 80-72 on all three scorecards.

Davis improved to 13-0 with ten knockouts, while Faccio fell to 10-2 with four knockouts.

Davis consistently attacked the body and controlled the action. He hurt Faccio with a body shot late in the seventh, but the Uruguayan remained on his feet.

Faccio fought back in an active final round, though Davis completed the shutout. Laurence Cole refereed.

Samuel Contreras Outpoints Oscar Pedroza Padilla

Samuel Contreras remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar “El Perro” Pedroza Padilla in their lightweight contest.

All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who improved to 9-0 with three knockouts. Pedroza Padilla dropped to 8-3-1 with three knockouts.

Contreras hurt Pedroza Padilla with a flurry midway through the second round, leaving him with a bloody nose. Pedroza Padilla answered with an overhand right that rocked Contreras during a competitive fourth.

Contreras finished strongly, landing the cleaner punches over the closing rounds to secure the decision. Angel Mendez refereed.

Daniel Cortez Edges Joshua Montoya

Daniel III Cortez won a six-round split decision over Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya in their super bantamweight bout.

Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third had Montoya ahead by the same score.

Cortez improved to 14-1 with nine knockouts, while Montoya fell to 8-6-2 with one knockout.

Cortez’s work rate helped him through several close rounds, but Montoya stayed competitive and finished well in the sixth. His late effort wasn’t enough to secure the verdict. Laurence Cole refereed.

Joseph Almajdi Defeats Miqal Dolphus

Joseph Almajdi defeated Miqal Dolphus by unanimous decision in their six-round super welterweight opener, winning 60-54 on all three cards.

Almajdi improved to 6-1 with three knockouts, while Dolphus suffered his first professional defeat and fell to 6-1-1 with four knockouts.

A right hand from Almajdi buzzed Dolphus near the end of the third round. Almajdi also landed a left hook late in the fifth that drove Dolphus backward, helping him complete a clear points victory.

Angel Mendez refereed. Ralph Velez Jr. handled the preliminary ring introductions, with Jimmy Lennon Jr. announcing the main card.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Targets O’Shaquie Foster After Undisputed Run
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson called for a future fight with O’Shaquie Foster after watching him defeat Emanuel Navarrete, describing the newly unified super featherweight champion as an opponent who would motivate him to return to the ring.

Shakur left the timing open, indicating he would wait until Foster finishes pursuing undisputed status at 130 pounds. His challenge came after Foster collected Navarrete’s WBO and IBF belts to go with his WBC championship Saturday night.

“Helluva fighter he will never give me my credit but I’ll be real tonight he showed his level,” Shakur wrote on X. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready.” He added: “I’ll be here after his undisputed run!”

Shakur’s challenge initially sounded immediate, but waiting until Foster becomes undisputed suggests he wants the fight to marinate before committing.

Foster earned the attention with a performance built on accurate counters, movement, and a strong finish. He dropped Navarrete twice in the 12th round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111.

That was the kind of opponent Shakur could appreciate: a boxer who made an aggressive, awkward champion miss and repeatedly punished him for reaching. Foster also recovered from being hurt late in the 11th to deliver his most decisive round.

There was a competitive edge beneath Shakur’s praise. His claim that Foster would never give him credit made the message more than a congratulatory post, although he still recognized what Foster had accomplished.

The practical questions remain unanswered. Shakur did not name a weight, propose a date, or suggest negotiations had begun. Foster has just secured three belts at super featherweight, while Shakur holds the WBO light welterweight title.

A meeting would therefore require decisions about weight as well as timing. For now, Shakur has identified Foster as a challenge worth pursuing, while giving him room to chase the remaining championship at 130 before discussing a fight.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Drops Emanuel Navarrete Twice To Unify
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster knocked Emanuel Navarrete down twice in the final round to complete a unanimous decision victory and unify three super featherweight titles Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The judges scored it 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111 for Foster, who retained his WBC belt and took Navarrete’s WBO and IBF championships. He also claimed the vacant Ring Magazine title in the DAZN main event.

Foster’s accuracy and movement frustrated Navarrete through much of the contest. He landed leaping left hooks early, followed with straight punches, and stepped away before Navarrete could bring his heavier attacks into play. Navarrete kept advancing but frequently found himself reaching and missing.

The third round offered Navarrete a route back into the fight. He caught Foster near the ropes, landed to the body, and threw a prolonged combination that forced the American onto defense. His pressure was more effective when he closed the distance before letting his hands go.

Foster adjusted in the fourth, taking the initiative with body jabs and counters. Over the middle rounds, he repeatedly beat Navarrete to the punch, landing straight shots and a sharp counter uppercut while using movement and clinches to interrupt the return attacks.

Navarrete remained dangerous despite struggling to sustain his offense. He landed some of his cleanest punches during a competitive tenth round, then hurt Foster with a heavy shot near the end of the 11th. That moment gave the closing stages an uncertainty the earlier rounds had often lacked.

Foster removed it in the 12th. With Navarrete chasing a knockout, Foster landed counter right hands that produced two knockdowns. Navarrete rose both times, but he couldn’t turn the fight around.

The finish strengthened a performance built on cleaner punching and better control of distance. Navarrete’s persistence kept him threatening late, but Foster made him pay for the risks he took and left with three world titles at 130 pounds.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete vs. O’Shaquie Foster Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Albert Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) knocked out Edward Vazquez (20-4, 6 KOs) with a second-round body attack to retain his NABF featherweight title. Gonzalez had a quiet opening round before increasing his aggression sharply in the second.

He hurt Vazquez early in the round and followed with short, compact combinations that left the challenger struggling to recover. Gonzalez kept attacking downstairs, landing heavy body punches, including a left hook, before Vazquez went to the canvas. Vazquez couldn’t beat the count, with referee Laurence Cole counting him out.

The unbeaten Gonzalez needed fewer than two rounds to defeat a former world title challenger in the scheduled ten-round co-main event. The knockout ended Vazquez’s three-fight winning streak and gave Gonzalez another early finish following his second-round victory over Aaron Alameda in July.

Frank “The Ghost” Martin (20-1-1, 14 KOs) stopped Tarik Zaina (18-4-1, 12 KOs) in the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title. Martin started cautiously, allowing the taller Zaina to keep the early rounds competitive with his reach and awkward style.

Zaina landed a couple of solid power shots in the third, giving Martin more to consider as he searched for openings. Through five rounds, Martin had yet to take firm control, with his opponent continuing to find occasional success at long range.

That changed in the seventh when Martin stepped back and dropped Zaina with a hard left hand. Zaina beat the count, but Martin immediately attacked with follow-up punches that forced the referee to stop the fight.

The finish handed Zaina his first stoppage defeat and gave Martin a needed victory after his February draw with Nahir Albright.

Deric “Scooter” Davis (13-0, 10 KOs) swept all eight rounds against Joaquin Silva Faccio (10-2, 4 KOs), winning a unanimous decision in their lightweight bout. All three judges scored it 80-72 for Davis, who controlled the action from the opening round.

Faccio came forward aggressively, but Davis picked him off with straight punches and used defensive movement to avoid much of the return fire. Davis continued landing the cleaner shots as Faccio’s awkward footwork did little to disrupt his accuracy.

In the sixth, Davis attacked the body with hard punches that left Faccio trying unsuccessfully to match his work. Faccio absorbed considerable punishment but kept fighting back through an active finish. There were no knockdowns, with Davis having to settle for a wide points victory against an opponent tough enough to last the distance.

Super bantamweight Daniel III Cortez (14-1, 9 KOs) edged Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya (8-6-2, 1 KO) by split decision. Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third favored Montoya by the same score. Cortez entered as the favorite but had to work for the victory against an opponent who kept the contest close.

Cortez’s busier work helped him in the third round, although Montoya came on toward the end of it. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, leaving the judges to separate them after six competitive rounds.

Montoya made a strong case for the decision, with ringside observer Francisco Salazar scoring the fight 58-56 in his favor. Cortez ultimately secured his 14th professional victory, but the divided scorecards reflected how little separated the two fighters.

Lightweight Samuel “Sammy” Contreras (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar Pedroza Padilla (8-3-1, 3 KOs). All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who controlled most of the action.

Contreras punished Pedroza Padilla through the first three rounds, leaving the Mexican fighter struggling to find an answer. Pedroza Padilla rallied in the fourth, getting inside and landing enough shots to draw a response from the crowd. Contreras regained control in the fifth, delivering more punishment and stopping his opponent from building on that success.

The fight went the distance without a knockdown, giving Contreras his ninth professional victory.

Joseph Almajdi (6-1, 3 KOs) handed Miqal Dolphus (6-1-1, 4 KOs) his first professional defeat, winning a six-round unanimous decision in their junior middleweight bout. All three judges scored the opening preliminary contest 60-54 for Almajdi.

Using his height and reach, Almajdi established distance with his jab and followed with straight right hands. Dolphus pressed forward and attacked the body, trying to get inside the taller fighter’s reach.

The middle rounds brought lively action, with Dolphus finding some success but Almajdi producing the cleaner work. Almajdi’s footwork and timing helped him control the distance often enough to sweep the scorecards.

Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Almajdi earning his sixth professional victory and Dolphus going the distance despite struggling to impose his pressure.

Sports.title: Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez In Two
Sports.content:
Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez broke through Edward Vazquez’s defenses with a punishing body attack, scoring a second-round knockout to retain his NABF featherweight title Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The unbeaten Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts in the scheduled ten-round co-main event on the Emanuel Navarrete–O’Shaquie Foster card on DAZN. Vazquez dropped to 20-4 with six knockouts, losing his three-fight winning streak.

Gonzalez gave little away about the approaching finish during a quiet opening round. The 24-year-old allowed Vazquez to be the more active fighter while taking time to find his distance. There was no sustained attack from Gonzalez, and the veteran challenger had an opportunity to get started without immediately being forced into survival mode.

That changed quickly in the second.

Gonzalez hurt Vazquez early and moved straight into his finishing work, throwing short combinations rather than giving the challenger time to recover. His punches downstairs did the most damage, with a left hook to the body among the blows that sent Vazquez to the canvas.

Referee Laurence Cole completed the ten-count with Vazquez unable to rise in time. Once Gonzalez increased his output, the fight went from a cautious start to a one-sided finish.

The result followed Gonzalez’s second-round body-shot knockout of Aaron Alameda in July, when he won the vacant NABF belt. Trained by Robert Garcia, Gonzalez again showed how quickly his compact punches can become decisive when an opponent remains within range.

Vazquez brought experience against Joe Cordina and Rafael Espinoza, along with recent winning form, but neither helped him absorb Gonzalez’s body attack. He had entered after three consecutive victories, including a decision over Daniel Lugo.

Gonzalez still needs tougher tests before his championship potential can be judged fully. This performance, however, gives his team reason to seek a higher-level opponent: Vazquez never had time to make his experience count once Gonzalez began landing heavily.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs Teofimo Lopez Targets February 6
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are targeting February 6 for their next fight, with negotiations continuing despite uncertainty over Lopez’s WBA title and Garcia’s pursuit of Floyd Mayweather Jr.

Mike Coppinger reports that neither the WBA’s decision nor the possibility of a Mayweather fight is expected to interfere with those discussions. That puts Garcia–Lopez ahead of the Mayweather matchup, which has generated plenty of talk without producing an agreement.

“Would be surprised if Garcia-Teofimo didn’t take place next,” Coppinger wrote on X. “Feb. 6 is the targeted date right now as talks continue.”

The date is still a target. There is no confirmed fight announcement, but the report gives Garcia’s next move a clearer direction after his attorney and adviser, Guadalupe Valencia, promoted the financial potential of facing Mayweather.

Valencia’s comments left the timetable dependent on Mayweather becoming available. Coppinger’s reporting places that possibility further down the road, with Teofimo first.

A Garcia–Lopez fight would give Ryan an opponent whose threat comes from what he can do today. Mayweather’s name would sell the event, but Teofimo offers a competitive fight between two active stars with something to lose.

The WBA situation remains a separate question. Jack Catterall has been pursuing his ordered fight with Lopez, while Teofimo has sought permission to pursue Garcia instead. Coppinger’s report indicates negotiations can continue regardless of the ruling; it does not establish whether Lopez will retain his championship.

That affects how the fight can eventually be promoted. Garcia–Lopez has an appeal with or without two belts, but calling it a confirmed unification would be premature until Lopez’s title position is settled.

Garcia also has reason to keep his attention on the opponent closest to becoming a reality. Selling a Mayweather fight before reaching terms with Teofimo risks making the more competitive matchup sound like a preliminary step.

For now, February 6 is the date to watch. Mayweather remains a possible later payday, while Garcia and Lopez work toward the fight Coppinger expects to happen next.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian fishermen recount how they survived on fresh fish when they got stranded at sea
Ghana News.content:
A 29-year-old Ghanaian fisherman has recounted how he and six colleagues survived nearly two weeks at sea after their canoe’s outboard motor broke down, leaving them without adequate food and drinking water.

Kwamena Nkum said the fishermen’s provisions ran out five days after the engine failure, forcing them to depend on fish they caught and eventually burn parts of their canoe to prepare meals.

The seven men, all from Sekondi, embarked on a fishing expedition to Axim in the Western Region on October 9, 2026, aboard a canoe named Second Chance.

Their journey took a dangerous turn three days later when the outboard motor stopped working. Efforts to repair the engine proved unsuccessful, leaving them stranded at sea.

“We usually spend five days at sea, but this time, our motor became faulty on the third day. It just went off. We tried to fix it, but it didn’t work. Our food and water got finished,” Mr Nkum recounted.

He said the fishermen resorted to drinking seawater after their supplies were exhausted, boiling it in an attempt to reduce its salt concentration.

They initially ate fish from their catch, but some of the fish spoiled and had to be discarded. The men subsequently used hooks and lines to catch fresh fish for food.

Mr Nkum said the fishermen had fuel and matches to make fire but eventually ran out of charcoal, compelling them to burn wood taken from their canoe to cook.

After drifting for several days, the men eventually sighted land during the night. One fisherman who was still awake alerted the others.

They switched on their mobile phones and later received a call from a friend, Kingsley, who was in contact with people back home.

Mr Nkum said they contacted their fishing leaders and attempted to establish their location. Although they initially believed they were in Togo, they later discovered they had drifted into Beninese waters.

“We had no food left. We were very hungry,” he said.

According to him, Kingsley and the fishing leaders contacted the chief fisherman in Benin, who provided the stranded men with food and water.

The fishermen subsequently received assistance from local fishing communities and the Beninese and Togolese navies.

They were eventually handed over to the Ghana Navy by a Togolese naval vessel at the Ghana-Togo maritime border on October 21, 2026.

The men later arrived safely at the Fishing Harbour in Tema following a joint search-and-rescue operation.

The fishermen were identified as Kofi Emmanuel, 32; Uncle Amoah, 45; Kwamena Nkum, 29; Kofi Aboagye, 36; Doboa, 35; Agya Badu, 42; and Kwamena Akyem, 40.

Reflecting on the ordeal, Mr Nkum said carrying a second outboard motor could have helped prevent the emergency from escalating, stressing the importance of having backup equipment for fishing expeditions.

Ghana News.title: Art can give ecological restoration a local voice – World Resources Institute
Ghana News.content:
The World Resources Institute (WRI) says art and culture can help make ecological restoration more meaningful to local communities.

This is according to the institute’s Landscape Restoration Manager for the Ghana Cocoa Belt, Eric Lartey, who made this known at the inaugural Climate x Culture Summit in Accra on Thursday, October 22.

“Restoration is more about people,” Mr Lartey said, explaining that music, oral traditions, festivals and customary practices shape how many Ghanaian communities relate to land, forests, water and biodiversity.

He said integrating culture can connect restoration to community identity and make use of traditional ecological knowledge, which “can also inform more effective restoration practices.”

Mr Lartey highlighted the Restoration Artists Network (RAN), a global initiative under the WRI that brings together musicians, visual artists, storytellers and cultural leaders to make ecological restoration more accessible.

“Artists are powerful storytellers and cultural influencers,” he said, describing their ability to translate technical restoration concepts into simple, engaging messages.

He cited a collaboration between Ghanaian and American artists that produced six songs drawing on Ghanaian musical traditions and local languages. The project aims to give landscape restoration “a local and a human voice,” he said.

“Art is an access point. It can invite attention, stimulate conversation,” Mr Lartey said.

He added that art can help people see themselves in a story that might otherwise feel technical or distant, while cautioning that it cannot replace investment, science or policy.

@theculturejoint Okyeame Kwame at the Climate x Culture Summit 2026 which brought together voices from sustainability, the creative industries and culture to explore how we can make climate action more practical, inclusive and part of everyday life. Together, we can turn creativity into climate action. ♬ original sound - Culture Joint

“If we want restoration effort to endure, it must be locally led and culturally grounded,” he said, pointing to Restore Local as a framework for the approach.

The summit, themed “Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences For Africa,” was organised by Culture Joint Media in partnership with Ghana’s Minister of State for Climate Change & Sustainability at the Presidency.

It brought together stakeholders from the climate, creative, business, media and technology sectors to explore how culture and creativity can contribute to climate action and sustainable development.

Ghana News.title: EPA takes Styrofoam ban campaign to five northern regions ahead of January 1, 2027 deadline
Ghana News.content:
The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) is intensifying its nationwide public education campaign on Ghana’s impending ban on polystyrene foam products, taking the campaign to five northern regions as the January 1, 2027, implementation deadline approaches.

The week-long campaign, scheduled for Monday, October 26, to Sunday, November 1, 2026, will cover the Northern, Upper East, Upper West, Savannah and North East regions, targeting consumers, manufacturers, distributors and other stakeholders ahead of the ban.

The EPA announced the ban on polystyrene foam products as part of efforts to address their environmental and adverse health impact and promote more sustainable alternatives. The nationwide awareness campaign is designed to prepare the public and industry players for the transition.

The campaign has been organised across three geographical zones; the southern belt, centred on Accra; the middle belt, centred on Kumasi; and the northern belt, centred on Tamale.

The Accra and Kumasi campaigns were held in July and August respectfully, with the Tamale campaign scheduled for October 29, 2026, bringing together stakeholders from all five northern regions for a major public awareness event.

Led by the EPA's Chief Executive Officer, Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse, the delegation will hold mini-durbars in Bolgatanga, Nalerigu, Damongo Wa among other communities thought the week before culminating the northern belt campaign in Tamale.

The Tamale event will feature an inter-school environmental quiz involving five second-cycle institutions namely the Ghana Senior High School, St. Charles Minor Seminary, Tamale Islamic Science Senior High School, Kalpohin Senior High School and Tamale Senior High School.

The competition will test students' knowledge of environmental issues, the health dangers associated with polystyrene foam products, their impact on the environment, the benefits of the ban and the lifestyle changes required before and after its implementation.

The initiative is expected to deepen environmental awareness among young people and encourage them to become advocates for responsible consumption and environmental protection.

The campaign will also feature a debate between the University for Development Studies (UDS) and Bagabaga College of Education under the motion;

BEYOND THE BAN: Can Ghana Turn the Polystyrene Foam Products Phase-Out into a Public Health, Environmental and Economic Benefits?

The UDS team will comprise Angela Ansah as principal speaker, Adu Michel Chibaley as supporting speaker, and Shakiratu Cheltima Fuseini as summarising speaker.

Bagabaga College of Education will be represented by Joseph Maadi Sagulo as principal speaker, Mbowura Clement Samira as supporting speaker, and Fuseini Abdul-Hakeem Tunteiya as summarising speaker.

The debate will provide a platform for the tertiary institutions to examine the implications of the ban and explore practical alternatives to polystyrene foam products.

Both institutions are also expected to showcase innovative alternative products they have developed to help bridge the supply gap that could emerge following the ban.

The event is expected to attract traditional authorities, school heads, students and other stakeholders. It will also be broadcast live across major television channels to extend its reach beyond the immediate audience.

Ahead of the main event, public awareness floats will be held in the five regional capitals to mobilise residents and draw attention to the impending ban.

The EPA will also intensify media engagements and stakeholder consultations throughout the week, while its regional, area and district offices have been directed to step up public education as the implementation date draws closer.

Speaking in an interview, EPA Chief Executive Officer Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse reaffirmed the Authority's commitment to ensuring effective implementation of the ban in accordance with the directive of President John Dramani Mahama.

She said the extensive public education campaign was intended to give consumers, manufacturers and distributors sufficient notice to prepare for the transition and adopt appropriate alternatives.

“The EPA is taking its time to create public awareness on the ban to prepare consumers, manufacturers and distributors for what is coming, effective January 1 2027, so they can prepare and make the right lifestyle adjustments."

“No one should have the excuse that they were not aware of this ban. There will be no excuses by January 2027. The EPA is fully ready to carry out His Excellency's orders to root this out from our country.”she added.

Other EPA officials are also on the ground leading various campaign teams, engaging communities and consulting relevant stakeholders on the impending restrictions.

With the January 1, 2027, deadline approaching, the Authority says it is stepping up public education to ensure that consumers and businesses understand the ban, prepare for the transition and embrace environmentally sustainable alternatives.

Ghana News.title: The betrayal of the ones we trusted
Ghana News.content:
There is a loneliness that has nothing to do with being alone. It is the loneliness of knocking on the door of the institution that was built for you, and hearing only the echo.

Ghana’s citizens are learning that loneliness this October.

Nineteen girls, and a house on the hill

At Obuasi Senior High Technical School, the number of students who have come forward with allegations of sexual abuse against the suspended headmaster has risen from 16 to 19, according to investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, who says more may follow because some did not report.

The allegations, which include rape, sexual assault and threats, are contained in his documentary. They remain subject to investigation. The headmaster has not been convicted of anything, and the Constitution says he is presumed innocent until proven guilty. That principle protects all of us, and I hold to it.

But presumption of innocence is a shield for the accused. It was never meant to be a blindfold for the system.

Look at what the reports say about who knew, and when. The Municipal Chief Executive for Obuasi has confirmed she was told last year, after a former sports master reported that the headmaster had slept with a student. A recording in the documentary reportedly captures the school’s housemistress describing how a female student was taken away at night after an allegation of sexual assault, and how the housemistress confronted the headmaster, who asked only how the girls were.

One political statement says some incidents were brought to school authorities as far back as March 2026, without meaningful action to protect the students. Reports also indicate the Ghana Education Service initially recommended only a transfer. A transfer would have moved the problem to another school. It would have done nothing to protect the girls already harmed, or the ones he might meet next.

Manasseh says this is not even his first visit to that school over such claims. By his account, his first visit, in 2018, was about allegations of sexual assault there too.

Only after the documentary did the machinery move. The Interior Minister told Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee that the police will conduct a thorough and impartial investigation, and that the matter will not be swept under the carpet. The headmaster resigned as constituency secretary of his political party and withdrew from its chairmanship race.

It is good that they moved. But why did it take a camera, a journalist and a national outcry? What was a child supposed to do in March, or in 2025, when she told the adults whose job it was to listen?

A girl who is abused by the person who holds the highest authority over her school has nowhere to run, because the system is built so that he is the one she must report to. When every door she knocks on opens onto someone who knows him, someone who fears him, or someone who votes with him, she learns something no child should learn. She learns that being believed is a privilege.

A student, a motorbike, and nineteen days

Ivan Apprey Baidoo was 20, a law student, on his way to play football. Prosecutors allege that a police corporal on traffic duty pursued the motorbike he was riding as a passenger, kicked it during the chase so that the rider lost control and crashed into a concrete barrier, and then left without arranging medical help.

Baidoo was pronounced dead on arrival. The corporal was charged with murder on 15 September, about three weeks after the 27 August incident. Those are the prosecution’s allegations, and the officer is entitled to his day in court.

I will say honestly that this case has seen movement. The officer was interdicted, the homicide unit took over, and charges were brought. But the family had to demand transparency, and a father had to say publicly that his son did not die in an ordinary accident. A young man who spent years studying the law died at the hands of someone who is paid to enforce it. Imagine what his mother thinks every time she hears the words “rule of law.”

“No bed”

Then there are those who die before the courts ever hear their names. On the night of 6 February, Charles Amissah, a 29-year-old engineer, was alive, stabilised and breathing. By dawn he was dead, after nearly three hours in an ambulance, denied admission at three of Accra’s most prominent hospitals because there was “no bed available”.

The investigating committee concluded that his death resulted from multiple system failures, including delays in emergency response, lack of proper stabilisation, and weak coordination between the major hospitals.

Nothing about this was new. In 2024, Korle Bu had to suspend referrals to its surgical and medical emergency unit because it was housing 60 patients in a 36-bed unit. Ghana’s ratio of roughly 0.9 hospital beds per 1,000 people is far below what the World Health Organization recommends. A person can fail by a system that never intended to hurt them. When failure is predictable, repeated and left uncorrected, it becomes a choice.

Due process is sacred. But justice delayed is justice denied, as every law student, including Ivan, was taught. A case that takes years leaves a victim waiting while her abuser keeps his title, his salary and his neighbors. It leaves a widow paying lawyers’ fees out of grief. In practice, the people who can afford to wait are the ones who need justice least.

That is how selective justice works. No one must announce it. It comes through who gets believed first, who gets a hearing, who can afford the lawyer, who has someone in the right office to call. The poor and the powerless are left with a thin version of the same Constitution.

The loneliest word in our language

Nineteen girls, a young man on a motorbike, an engineer in an ambulance. Different stories, one feeling. The people who trusted us to be ready, to be fair and to be fast found that the door was shut.

If we want to repair this, we must start by honoring what the Constitution says quickly. Investigate the Obuasi allegations transparently and protect the girls who spoke from retaliation. Create independent reporting channels in every school. Make emergency care a legal duty that does not depend on a vacant bed.

Hold officers to the same law they enforce on everyone else. And let no victim in Ghana ever again must wait for a journalist before an institution decides to care.

So, what is freedom, if a girl is not free from fear in her own school? What is justice, if it must be asked for in the right accent, from the right family, with the right lawyer and the right party card? Freedom is not only the absence of chains. It is the confidence that if someone breaks you, the state will stand on your side of the room.

We are better than this. But only if we act like it.

Ghana News.title: Bookworm urges schools to embrace extracurricular activities to develop pupils’ talents
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Bookworm, Nelson Kofi Poku, has urged parents and teachers to encourage children to participate in extracurricular activities to help them develop their talents and improve their chances of accessing educational opportunities.

He said academic performance in the classroom alone was no longer sufficient to prepare children for the opportunities available in an increasingly competitive world.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Bookworm Greater Accra Season 13 grand finale on Saturday, October 24, Mr Poku said educational competitions and other public activities provided platforms for children to demonstrate their abilities and attract opportunities beyond the classroom.

“We are living in a society where your performance in the classroom alone is not enough to excel,” he said.

He encouraged parents and teachers to expose children to activities that would build their confidence, improve their communication skills and enable them to showcase their abilities.

Mr Poku cited the example of a female student from Keta in the Volta Region who, according to him, made history by reaching the final stage of a National Science and Maths Quiz competition, an achievement that helped her secure an opportunity to continue her education abroad.

He said such opportunities demonstrated the importance of allowing children to participate in competitions that could open doors to further education and personal development.

“Parents and teachers should adapt this kind of learning and enrol children in public activities. By so doing, society will begin to know what the children have and what they can offer,” he said.

Bookworm expands educational competition

Mr Poku said Bookworm, which has operated for nearly a decade, had expanded its activities to about 10 regions across the country.

He disclosed that the Greater Accra competition began with approximately 74 schools, with 33 qualifying for the grand finale.

The competition, held on October 24, featured three categories: lower primary, upper primary and junior high school (JHS), with winners to be crowned in each division.

He said the Greater Accra event was the third regional finale organised by the programme in October, following competitions in the Eastern Region on October 10 and the Ashanti Region on October 16.

According to him, Bookworm remains open to pupils from both public and private schools, providing an opportunity for children from different educational backgrounds to participate.

He described the participation of public schools as encouraging, noting that the programme was designed to accommodate all interested pupils.

“We open our hands to all students. Anyone who develops an interest in joining the programme is welcome. We take them through the process, and we do it together,” he said.

Scholarships, laptops and international exposure

Mr Poku said Bookworm had introduced incentives to reward outstanding participants and motivate children to improve their academic and personal development.

He explained that winners receive 50 per cent scholarships for one year, while ultimate winners are also presented with laptops.

Additionally, sponsors support selected top performers to undertake trips to Dubai, covering 50 per cent of the cost, with the level of support varying according to their positions in the competition.

He said the international exposure was intended to broaden the children's perspectives and introduce them to opportunities and experiences beyond Ghana.

Mr Poku added that corporate partners, including Trillium Industry, Choco and Floral Tissue, also provide souvenirs and other items for participants and winners.

Beyond reading and comprehension

The Bookworm CEO said the competition was designed to develop a broad range of skills rather than focus solely on reading.

He explained that participants undergo several stages, including storytelling, summarising passages and answering comprehension questions.

Another segment, known as Knowing Your Parents, is designed to strengthen relationships between children and their parents by helping them understand their family backgrounds, preferences and behaviour.

Mr Poku said the segment was introduced to encourage parents to spend more time with their children and strengthen family bonds.

He expressed confidence that the different activities would help participants develop critical thinking, communication and interpersonal skills while building their confidence.

He said Bookworm would continue to provide platforms through which children could discover their strengths, demonstrate their abilities and prepare for future opportunities.

Ghana News.title: Bookworm crowns winners of 2026 schools competition in Accra
Ghana News.content:
Bookworm has crowned winners in three categories of its 2026 schools competition following a grand finale held in Accra on Saturday, October 24.

Isabela Ayidah of Hertford International Christian School emerged winner in the upper primary category with a score of 96.43 per cent, while Godiva Koomson of Hallmark International School won the lower primary category with 96.50 per cent.

In the junior high school category, Tsevi Othnel of Charlotte Memorial School emerged winner with 93.50 per cent.

The competition, organised to promote reading, comprehension and communication skills among schoolchildren, brought together 33 schools for the Greater Accra grand finale.

Speaking after the event, the Chief Executive Officer of Bookworm, Nelson Kofi Poku, said the initiative was aimed at helping children develop their talents and build confidence beyond conventional classroom learning.

He urged parents and teachers to encourage pupils to participate in educational competitions and other extracurricular activities, saying these platforms could expose them to opportunities for further education and personal development.

“We are living in a society where your performance in the classroom alone is not enough to excel,” he said.

Mr Poku explained that Bookworm had operated for nearly a decade and expanded its activities to about 10 regions across Ghana.

The Greater Accra finale was the third regional competition organised by the initiative in October, following events in the Eastern Region on October 10 and the Ashanti Region on October 16.

He said the programme was open to pupils from both public and private schools, with the aim of providing an inclusive platform for children to demonstrate their abilities.

The competition featured several stages, including storytelling, summarising passages and answering comprehension questions. A segment known as Knowing Your Parents was also designed to strengthen relationships between children and their parents.

Mr Poku said winners receive 50 per cent scholarships for one year, while ultimate winners are also awarded laptops.

Selected top performers also benefit from sponsorship arrangements covering 50 per cent of the cost of trips to Dubai, providing opportunities for international exposure.

He said the initiative would continue to support children's academic development, nurture their talents and equip them with skills that could help them excel in the future.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Tennis Federation congratulates Wheelchair champions after Ga Mantse Tournament
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Tennis Federation (GTF) has congratulated wheelchair tennis players and officials for their commitment, sacrifice and participation in the Ga Mantse Tennis Tournament, highlighting the growing development of wheelchair tennis in Ghana.

The tournament featured competitive men’s and women’s wheelchair tennis divisions, providing athletes with an opportunity to showcase their skills, resilience and sportsmanship.

In the men’s division, Bernard Yawson emerged champion, while Daniel Laryea finished as runner-up. In the women’s division, Stacy Konadu Mensah claimed the title, with Bridget Nartey finishing as runner-up.

The Federation commended all four finalists and every participating athlete for contributing to an exciting and competitive tournament.

The GTF expressed its appreciation to the organisers, Abusua, for including wheelchair tennis in the Ga Mantse Tennis Tournament.

According to the Federation, initiatives of this nature are essential to the development of para sport in Ghana, as they provide athletes with valuable competition, greater public visibility and opportunities to assess their progress.

The Federation also expressed hope that future editions of the tournament would be bigger and create an even greater impact on wheelchair tennis development.

Speaking on behalf of the Board, Henry K. N. Larbi, National Coordinator of Ghana Wheelchair Tennis, congratulated the players and officials for their dedication and commitment to the sport.

He stressed the importance of securing sponsorship to enable Ghanaian wheelchair tennis players to compete in international tournaments and improve their chances of qualifying for the LA2028 Paralympic Games.

Larbi noted that despite the talent and determination demonstrated by the athletes, limited financial resources remain a major obstacle to their international participation.

Qualification for the Paralympic Games in wheelchair tennis depends significantly on international rankings, which players build through participation in recognised tournaments.

However, the cost of international travel, accommodation, tournament entry fees and specialised sports wheelchairs continues to pose a challenge for Ghanaian athletes.

With the LA2028 Paralympic Games approaching, the Ghana Tennis Federation is appealing to corporate organisations, government agencies, development partners and individuals to support the country’s wheelchair tennis players.

Beyond competition, the Federation believes wheelchair tennis plays an important role in promoting inclusion, building confidence and changing public perceptions of persons with disabilities.

The Ghana Tennis Federation and Ghana Wheelchair Tennis have reaffirmed their commitment to expanding the sport nationwide, identifying emerging talent and creating opportunities for athletes to compete at the highest level.

Ghana News.title: MUSIGA warns musicians against glorifying online fraud
Ghana News.content:
The Musicians Union of Ghana (MUSIGA) has cautioned musicians against making public statements that could be interpreted as encouraging or glorifying online fraud and other cyber-related crimes.

In a statement signed by its President, Bessa Simons, MUSIGA said it respected musicians’ right to express opinions on governance, unemployment, corruption and the administration of justice, but stressed that such concerns should not be used to justify criminal conduct.

“While MUSIGA respects every musician’s right to express opinions on governance, unemployment, corruption, and the fair administration of justice, we state emphatically that no grievance against public institutions justifies statements that may appear to normalize fraud, portray suspected offenders as heroes, or discourage cooperation with lawful investigations,” the statement said.

The Union’s statement follows comments Shatta Wale made during ShattaFest in Accra on 17 October 2026, which suggested that he was encouraging young people to engage in fraud.

“Me I do my music for over 25 years. I buy Rolls Royce, I buy Lamborghini all from my music. Then somebody go go talk somebody say Shatta Wale he dey do fraud.

“Make I tell you today. I get plenty fraud boys who be my friends but me I no be snitch wey I go snitch anybody. The country no good so if you go fraud, fraud,” he said in Pidgin English.

Shatta Wale’s comments have since generated widespread discussion, with some critics expressing concern that his influence could negatively affect society, particularly young people.

MUSIGA warned that online fraud causes real harm to victims, damages Ghana’s international reputation, threatens legitimate digital businesses and endangers the future of young people.

It therefore urged musicians, particularly those with large followings and influence among young people, to avoid statements, performances and social media posts that could be construed as promoting or defending internet fraud, money laundering, romance scams, identity theft and other forms of cybercrime.

“Musicians must understand that their words carry weight. A stage, concert platform, interview, or social-media account is not a private space; it is a powerful channel of public influence,” the statement added.

The Union said using such platforms to excuse criminal conduct, attack lawful enforcement actions or indirectly encourage fraudulent activities was irresponsible and inconsistent with the values of the music profession.

However, MUSIGA acknowledged that concerns about selective justice, corruption, youth unemployment and accountability were legitimate national issues that musicians had every right to raise.

It maintained that criticism of public institutions and demands for justice should be pursued constructively without appearing to endorse unlawful behaviour.

“However, criticism of injustice must never become a justification for crime,” the statement stressed.

The Union called on artistes to channel their influence towards addressing the challenges confronting young people by advocating employment opportunities, supporting digital-skills training, promoting financial literacy and entrepreneurship, and speaking out against corruption and fraud.

It urged the music industry to contribute to solutions that would help young people pursue lawful and productive livelihoods rather than expose themselves to criminal activities.

MUSIGA also cautioned musicians against making statements that could expose them or their fans to legal, reputational or professional consequences.

“Every musician must remember that fame does not place them above the law, and artistic freedom does not include the freedom to encourage unlawful conduct,” the statement said.

The Union reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the rights and welfare of musicians but warned that it would not remain silent when public statements by members threatened the credibility of the profession and the safety of Ghanaian youth.

It called on musicians to use their platforms responsibly, defend the dignity of Ghana’s creative industry and inspire young people to pursue success through lawful and productive means.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi barrage near Mecca
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels launch a barrage of missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia, triggering widespread civil defence alerts and international condemnation.

The Saudi-led coalition has intercepted a barrage of projectiles from Yemen that targeted cities across the kingdom.

Saudi Civil Defence said that shrapnel from two intercepted ballistic missiles, suspected to have been fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, fell in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh, and Wadi Al-Mughammas in Mecca province.

A drone and ballistic missile were also intercepted over the Saudi capital Riyadh during the barrage, which began Saturday evening.

By midday Sunday, coalition forces had intercepted a cruise missile targeting Khamis Mushait, with warning sirens blaring out across Taif and Jazan. In total, 10 ballistic missiles directed at the southern region were intercepted.

Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed AlBudaiwi said the strikes represented “a grave violation of the sanctity of the Holy Sites and a provocation to the sentiments of Muslims worldwide”, referring to the interceptions in Mecca, home of the Kaaba and Masjid al-Haram. The Houthis, a Zaydi Shia group, have denied targeting Muslim holy sites in Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom has faced waves of Houthi missile and drone strikes in recent weeks, targeting civilian and military infrastructure.

Riyadh announced late Saturday that international flights from King Khalid International Airport would resume from Terminal 2 on Sunday, while Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights.

This follows the suspension of flights from the Riyadh airport after waves of Houthi strikes, including one on October 10 that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds.



Early Sunday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned civilians away from the Saudi capital’s airport.

“King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh is not safe because it is a military target, and we renew our warning to airlines, employees, and travelers,” Saree stated. He also announced seven operations targeting Saudi oil facilities and military bases.

Yemen has been in a state of war since Houthi forces captured the capital Sanaa in September 2014, forcing the government to flee south.

After a brief ceasefire, fighting in Yemen has intensified after government forces attacked Sanaa International Airport to prevent a Houthi delegation arriving from Tehran.

The Houthis then launched a surprise offensive in September, capturing Yemen’s western coast, including the city of Mocha.

Forces aligned with the internationally recognised government launched “Operation Dawn of Yemen” on October 5, aimed at retaking territories lost to the Houthis.

On Sunday, Yemen’s armed forces said the military had carried out 736 strikes on Houthi positions over the past 24 hours, leading to 307 people being “neutralised” and the destruction of 68 military vehicles.

Amid the military escalation, the Rasd Organization for Rights and Freedoms has warned of the dire humanitarian situation in the city of Taiz, which is under a Houthi siege.

“About 1,110 kidney failure patients face the risks of a shortage of dialysis supplies, given the need for about 120 dialysis sessions daily along with 192 patients in intensive care units and 154 children in incubators, due to the Houthi siege imposed on the city of Taiz since October 4,” the group said.

World.title: Gaza’s visually and hearing-impaired children miss school due to Israel war
World.content:
Children in Gaza with auditory and visual challenges often have no access to specialist education.

Gaza City – With the help of his father, 13-year-old Kenan al-Sabaa attempts to adjust his hearing aid, which has malfunctioned. The plastic tubing and rubber ear mould on the device need fixing, but these parts and the depleted batteries are no longer available due to Israel’s siege on the Gaza Strip.
