Nigeria deserves leaders who understand that mental health is a national development issue, leaders who speak with empathy, legislate with wisdom, and act with urgency. Leaders who know that when someone reaches the point of giving up, survival should be celebrated not prosecuted.

To paraphrase Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong’s view: When a person gets to the point of throwing in the towel and tries to end it all, we should protect, support, and never punish. The future of this nation depends on how seriously we take the mental wellbeing of its people. It is past time for our lawmakers to rise to that responsibility. Governance should never laugh at pain, and policies must not criminalise suffering, they should strengthen systems that uphold healthcare, dignity, and protection from despair. It may also be worth exploring a functional‑fitness assessment for anyone seeking political office to ensure those entrusted with millions of lives have the judgment, cognitive capacity, and emotional regulation required for public responsibility.

We cannot rewrite the past, but we can choose a kinder future. A future where survival is honoured, vulnerability is supported, and every Nigerian knows their life is worth holding on to.

Margaret Uddin Ojeahere is the founder of Noetic Minders Health Initiative and a consultant psychiatrist with Jos University Teaching Hospital, Plateau State, Nigeria.

World.title: Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos
World.content:
A mother and her child have died after two container-laden trucks overturned at Mile 2, near Freeman Market, inward Apapa, Lagos.

Vanguard newspaper reported on Sunday that the victims were trapped beneath the trucks and their containers in the accident, which occurred over the weekend.

The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said its rescue team evacuated the victims and cleared the wreckage. Traffic was diverted through an adjoining service lane while a crane and a heavy-duty tow vehicle were used to remove the overturned trucks and containers. Police officers secured the scene during the operation.

The victims’ remains were taken to the police mortuary in Yaba.

LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, called for an investigation to determine the cause of the crash, including whether mechanical faults, overloading, improper cargo distribution or driver negligence played a role.

He urged truck operators to ensure their vehicles were roadworthy and their loads properly secured.

The accident comes weeks after another crash involving two trucks, a commercial bus and nine motorcycles at First Gate, inward Mile 2, along the Mile 2-Seme Expressway, left four people critically injured.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 6 October crash involved two Mack trucks, one carrying a 20-foot container. LASTMA said preliminary findings suggested that one of the trucks might have suffered brake failure, causing the driver to lose control and collide with the other vehicles.

The injured victims, three men and a woman, sustained multiple fractures to their arms and legs and were taken to hospital for treatment.

LASTMA said the drivers involved in that crash were handed over to the police for investigation and possible prosecution.

The cause of the latest accident has not been established.

World.title: NDLEA arrests South African woman with 36.65kg cocaine, Lagos car dealer
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a South African woman with 36.65kg of cocaine at Lagos airport and a Lagos-based car dealer accused of receiving and arranging accommodation for her.

The agency also arrested a Nigerian-American woman with 9.45kg of cannabis known as loud after she arrived in Nigeria from the United States.

In a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday, NDLEA spokesperson Femi Babafemi identified the South African woman as Qhina Beauty, 34.

He explained that she was arrested on 7 October at the departure hall of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, Lagos, while preparing to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha.

A search of her two bags uncovered 30 blocks of cocaine weighing 36.65kg, the NDLEA said, adding that the drugs were wrapped in Sellotape, divided into seven parcels and laced with dried pepper.

Ms Beauty reportedly told investigators that she arrived in Nigeria on 30 September to collect the consignment. She said another South African woman recruited her and promised to pay her 20,000 rand after delivery.

She also identified two other people allegedly involved in the operation: one based in the United States and the other a Lagos car dealer, the statement said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The agency said it arrested the dealer, Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, 46, on 14 October at Apple Junction, Ago Palace Way, Lagos, after keeping him under surveillance at his residence in Shasha.

Mr Umunnakwe reportedly admitted receiving Ms Beauty at the airport and arranging her stay at Santiago Hotel in Amuwo-Odofin.

The agency noted that he later moved her to Cynarisso Hotel near the airport ahead of her departure.

Previous cocaine seizure

The arrests come about two months after the NDLEA announced the seizure of 184.5kg of cocaine, valued at an estimated N39 billion, in Lagos.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the cocaine was intercepted while being prepared for export through a courier logistics company. The operation led to the arrests of Kazeem Afolabi, popularly known as KC Luxury, and Lawal Kehinde, a logistics company employee.

The NDLEA described Mr Afolabi as the alleged Nigerian coordinator of an international drug trafficking syndicate.

It said the network used Nigeria as a transit point to move cocaine from South America to the United Kingdom, other parts of Europe and Asia.

The agency described the seizure as the largest interception of cocaine through a courier channel in its history.

Nigerian-American woman arrested with cannabis

In a separate operation, NDLEA operatives arrested Anetor Gloria Ubong, 62, a realtor based in Richmond, Texas, at Lagos airport on 21 October after she arrived on a United Airlines flight from Houston.

Ms Ubong, who holds Nigerian and United States passports, had 18 parcels of Loud weighing 9.45kg in one of her two checked-in boxes. The drugs were concealed in a box covered with gift-wrapping paper.

According to the agency, she told investigators that her daughter and her daughter’s future brother-in-law had delivered the box to her home in the US. She said she was to deliver it in Nigeria to her daughter’s fiancé, identified as Jibola.

In another operation in Lagos, a special unit of the agency arrested Eletu Rasheedat, 41, in the Eti Osa area on 23 October.

The operatives recovered 5,820 pills of diazepam, 780 tablets of tramadol, 3.7kg of skunk and 230.25 litres of skuchies.

Seizures across other states

In Delta State, operatives arrested Peter Ugochukwu, 51, in Warri and recovered thousands of opioid capsules and tablets, bottles of codeine syrup and other substances.

The seizures included 29,350 capsules of tramadol, 6,620 tablets of tramadol 200mg, 4,116 bottles of codeine syrup, 11,340 tablets of Rohypnol and 3,500 tablets of diazepam.

Officers also recovered 300 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 200 ampoules of diazepam injection, and quantities of tramadol 225mg, Molly and Cocodamol.

The NDLEA said the suspect and a white Hummer bus were handed over to the agency by the Nigeria Police Force in Delta State.

In a separate operation at Enhere Junction, Warri, officers arrested Helen Bakporo Samson, 46, on 19 October with 6kg of skunk.

In Oyo State, operatives arrested Fajana Dada Oluwaseyi, 41, in the Adamasingba area of Ibadan on 19 October. The agency said he had escaped arrest after officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis from his house on 16 September.

In Kano State, a raid in Gerawa on 22 October led to the arrest of Murtala Lawan, 30, and the seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis weighing 97.2kg.

In Taraba State, operatives arrested Raiyanu Misa, 39, at the Lankaviri checkpoint in Yorro Local Government Area on 23 October with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg.

On the same day, the police handed over another suspect to the NDLEA after arresting him at Dakka village in Bali Local Government Area with 112 blocks of cannabis weighing 81.49kg.

In Niger State, officers arrested Emmanuel Ekene, 26, on the Sabo-Kainji Road in Borgu Local Government Area on 19 October with 64,000 opioid pills, including tramadol and diazepam.

In Bauchi State, operatives arrested Jamilu Mustapha, also known as Last Card, 45, at Nasaru Town in Ningi Local Government Area on 21 October. They recovered 379kg of cannabis packed in seven sacks.

NDLEA destroys cannabis farms in Ondo, Edo

In Ondo State, operatives raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, on 20 October and recovered 56 abandoned bags of cannabis weighing 583kg.

In Edo State, the agency destroyed two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West Local Government Area, on 18 October. The farms had an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg.

The operatives burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took another 97kg as exhibits.

In a separate operation at Ewe community in Owan West, officers arrested Mary Edokhai, 42, with 35kg of cannabis.

The NDLEA chairman, Buba Marwa, commended the officers involved in the operations and urged them to sustain efforts against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

The agency also said its commands continued public awareness campaigns under its War Against Drug Abuse programme, including sessions for students and school staff.

World.title: Lagos SWAN inaugurates seven-member electoral committee ahead of elections
World.content:
The Lagos State chapter of the Sports Writers Association of Nigeria (SWAN) has inaugurated a seven-member electoral committee to organise elections for a new executive committee.

The committee, known as the SWAN Electoral Committee (SWANECO), was inaugurated on Friday at the Teslim Balogun Stadium, Surulere, Lagos, during the chapter’s Extraordinary Congress.

Patrick Omorodion, chairman of the chapter’s caretaker committee, inaugurated the electoral body, which is chaired by Mozez Praiz, with McAnthony Anaelechukwu as secretary.

Other members are Abdul Rahmone Abulore, Soliu Adeyemo, Tega Onajaife, Jovita Ekeh and Suo Chapele.

Mr Omorodion said the committee’s establishment was part of the mandate given to the caretaker committee by the national body to strengthen the chapter’s administration and facilitate a credible election.

He said the process was intended to help restore stability and ensure the chapter had a substantive executive committee.

Speaking on behalf of the electoral committee, Mr Praiz pledged to carry out the assignment responsibly and help usher in a new executive committee capable of revitalising the chapter.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He cited activities such as the now-dormant SWAN Cup as examples of initiatives the chapter could revive to strengthen its engagement with members.

Enitan Obadina, SWAN’s national welfare officer, who represented the national executive at the congress, described the inauguration as a positive development for the Lagos chapter.

“As one of the country’s leading chapters, we are happy that Lagos is on the right path, and national SWAN, led by its president, Isaiah Benjamin, is providing support to ensure the process follows the constitution and is inclusive for members, to avoid the challenges of the past,” he said.

Veterans of the association who attended the ceremony included Mitchel Obi, Kunle Solaja, Felix Awogu, Godwin Enakhena, Emma Jemegah, Joe Apu, Pius Ayinor, Mike Mayaki and Smart Ebhodaghe.

The national body established the Lagos SWAN caretaker committee on 9 October with Mr Omorodion as chairman, Oni Afolabi as secretary and Anulika Menanya as a member.

The electoral committee is expected to oversee the process of electing a new executive for the Lagos chapter.

World.title: EPL: Carrick bench Bruno Fernandes after Como outburst
World.content:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said it was a “pure football” decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench despite the Portugal midfielder’s criticism of his manager’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como.

Without a win in seven games in all competitions, Carrick badly needs a victory against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to quell speculation over his future and has made a bold call.

The Red Devils begin the day 15th in the table with just seven points from their opening seven league games.

Fernandes hit out at United’s passive approach out of possession as Champions League debutants Como ran riot in Italy on Wednesday.

“When you have options it’s always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want,” added Carrick as he dismissed the decision was taken as a response to Fernandes’s outburst.

Fernandes won a clean sweep of individual awards last season after breaking the Premier League record for assists with 21 as United finished third in the table.

But the 32-year-old’s impact has been much more limited so far this season, bar a hat-trick against Ipswich back in August.

Carrick made four changes in total with Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui also dropping out for Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo.

Fernandes’s comments came just over a week after Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s board for not doing enough to strengthen Carrick’s squad in the transfer window.

Martinez was not dropped for his remarks but was replaced at half-time in a 1-1 draw at Leeds last weekend with an injury and is only fit enough to return from the bench against Bournemouth.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players,” said United’s all-time leading goalscorer Wayne Rooney.

He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.”

Vanguard News

World.title: FRSC identifies persistent safety violations among tanker drivers
World.content:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has identified speeding, driver fatigue, overloading and driving against traffic as persistent violations among petroleum tanker drivers.

The FRSC spokesman, Osondu Ohaeri who told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Abuja, warned that such practices continue to threaten road safety despite enforcement efforts.

Ohaeri further discussed the challenges associated with the transportation of petroleum products and other goods by articulated vehicles.

He said some tanker drivers exceeded recommended speed limits in attempts to meet delivery schedules, despite the difficulty of bringing heavily loaded vehicles to a safe stop.

He explained that the size and weight of tankers required drivers to exercise caution, particularly when approaching bridges, bends and congested sections of highways.

He also identified fatigue as a major risk, noting that some drivers attempted to cover long distances, including journeys from Kano to Lagos, overnight without adequate rest.

“Driving while fatigued could impair concentration and reaction time, increasing the likelihood of losing control of vehicles.

“Also, driving against traffic is another serious violation. Some operators overload their vehicles or use them to carry additional goods alongside petroleum products.

“These practices can compromise vehicle stability and expose drivers, passengers and other road users to danger,” he said.

Ohaeri attributed the persistence of the violations partly to drivers’ attitudes and the pressure to meet delivery schedules, stressing that compliance with traffic regulations remained essential regardless of operational demands.

He said the FRSC had continued to intensify safety education and enforcement while working with operators and other stakeholders to improve compliance.

He disclosed that the corps had achieved about 75 per cent success in issuing the appropriate Class G driver’s licences to relevant operators, as part of efforts to ensure that drivers possessed the required qualifications.

He said the agency was also engaging petroleum marketers and other industry stakeholders to strengthen safety standards across the transportation chain.

He urged tanker drivers and operators to prioritise safety over delivery schedules, warning that violations involving vehicles conveying highly flammable products could have devastating consequences.

He called for improved driver discipline, adequate rest, proper vehicle maintenance and strict adherence to speed limits to reduce crashes involving articulated vehicles.

World.title: Police rescue kidnap victim in Oyo
World.content:
police badge

The Police Command in Oyo State has neutralised a suspected kidnapper and rescued a 15-year-old kidnapped victim during a coordinated security operation along the Awe–Iwo Road area in the state.

The Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade disclosed this in a statement on Sunday in Ibadan.

Ayanlade said that the successful operation reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to combating kidnapping and other violent crimes through intelligence-led policing.

The PPRO said that the operation followed credible intelligence received by the Command on Thursday at about 5:00 p.m that suspected kidnappers were demanding ransom for the release of a kidnapped victim.

According to him, the kidnapped victim was abducted from the Onidundun area of Akinyele Local Government Area on Oct.18.

“Upon receipt of the intelligence, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Olugbenga, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Section (AKS), working in close collaboration with Oyo Zone Vigilante Group of Nigeria, to move against the suspects and secure the victim’s release.

“Consequently, the operatives mobilised to the Pipeline, Ajagba axis along the Awe–Iwo Road, where they advanced on the suspects’ location.

“At about 9:30 p.m the operation resulted in a gun duel after the suspected kidnappers opened fire upon sighting the advancing security team,” he said.

Ayanlade said that the successful operation led to the rescue of the kidnapped victim, identified as Sumaila Muhammadu, a 15-year-old male.

He said that a yet-to-be-identified suspected kidnapper was neutralised while other members of the gang fled in different directions with gunshot injuries.

Ayanlade said that the neutralised suspect was taken to the Hospital, where he was confirmed dead by a medical doctor and his corpse subsequently deposited at the morgue.

According to him, police operatives recovered one Android mobile phone and a cutlass during the operation and efforts currently ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects.

He urged residents of the community to be calm and promptly report anyone with suspicious gunshot wounds to the Police.

Ayanlade further urged medical practitioners, hospital administrators, and other healthcare workers to promptly notify the Police of anyone seeking treatment for gunshot injuries.

World.title: Nigerian student dies after asthma attack while celebrating birthday with friends in London
World.content:
A 26-year-old Nigerian international student, Obanyeli Jesse Chima, has died after suffering an asthma attack while preparing to celebrate his birthday with friends in London.

Chima had recently completed his master’s degree in Public Health and was awaiting graduation when the incident occurred.

According to MyLondon, the incident happened on Saturday, September 19, when Chima met his friend, Eva, and her partner to celebrate their birthdays, which fell on consecutive days.

While waiting in a lounge, Chima reportedly told Eva that he needed to step outside for some air because he was experiencing an asthma attack.

He began struggling to breathe and used three inhalers he had with him, but they failed to provide relief.

Eva called an ambulance, but Chima collapsed while she was speaking to the emergency operator.

Eva told MyLondon: “Our friend started CPR after being guided by the ambulance operators. Multiple ambulances came, and they spent around two hours working on him to stabilise his heart. They finally got him to the hospital and told us he’s on life support. They said he might only have memory loss, but he will be fine.

“Two days later, they said he’s not getting better. There was no improvement. They eventually did a brain test on him and confirmed that he was brain-dead. On September 25, we lost him. It’s horrible because we were just laughing, and four days later, we had to see his lifeless body.”

She said the gathering had been planned as an opportunity for the friends to celebrate their birthdays together, as all three had birthdays in September.

“The weekend he suffered was the only weekend we all had free – all our birthdays are in September. He, my partner, and I all have our birthdays one day after another. That weekend was our chance to hang out, but instead we ended up at the hospital.”

Chima had recently completed his master’s degree in Public Health and was looking forward to his graduation.

“His family had saved money for his graduation, and now that money needs to be used to bury their child. It’s horrible”, Eva continued.

Chima and Eva became friends after leaving Nigeria to study in London. He had also worked at Chelsea Football Club, the team he supported.

Eva described him as a ‘beloved and cherished friend who was the life of the party’.

Despite being described as physically fit, his sudden death shocked his friends, who had not anticipated such an outcome.

Chima leaves behind three siblings in Nigeria, where his family is making arrangements to bring his body home for burial.

To support the grieving family, Eva and her friends have launched a fundraising campaign to cover the cost of transporting his body to Nigeria, alongside mortuary fees and other related expenses.

Explaining the reason for the fundraiser, Eva said: “We’re trying our best to see what we can raise. His family were planning for graduation. As international students, it’s tough already. We want to help take the burden off his family. Nobody has money saved up to bury a child.

“His dad made enquiries about burying him in the UK but most of his family is in Nigeria. The family want to see his body before they lay him to rest, so returning him to Nigeria makes more sense; he should be closer to home.”

Eva hopes to raise between £7,000 and £9,000 to cover the costs of repatriating Chima’s body to Nigeria.

Vanguard News

World.title: We’ll not backdate resignations after our letter to INEC – NNPP
World.content:
The New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) says it will not give in to blackmail of backdating the resignation of members elected on its platform , who failed to complete the process before its letter to INEC on the issue.

The party also warned those approaching some members of its leadership to desist as falsifying the records is tantamount to criminality.

This is contained in a statement signed by its Founder and Chairman Board of Trustees,

Dr Boniface Aniebonam on Sunday.

The NNPP insisted that those approaching it now to backdate their incomplete resignation will not be accommodated for obvious reasons.

The party was reacting to controversy within its ranks that some of its elected members affected by the letter to INEC have approached the leadership to backdate their resignation.

Recall that the NNPP in a letter to INEC on Monday, Oct. 19, stated that Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State, 18 members of the House of Representatives , 28 members of the State House of Assembly from Kano, and 2 Senators elected on its platform in 2023, did not complete the constitutional requirements for resignation from the party.

The letter, which was jointly signed by the NNPP National Chairman, Dr Agbo Major and General Secretary , Mr Oginni Olaposi stated that the members, who are now in other political parties and contesting for the 2027 general elections have not complied with the constitutional requirements governing resignation from the NNPP.

“We write to formally inform the commission of the purported resignation and subsequent political activities of certain elected public office holders, who obtained their respective mandates on the platform of our great party but have failed to comply with prescribed procedures for lawful termination of their membership.”

The NNPP leadership assured its members that it will not give in to pressure to reconsider those who left without due process or give in to pressure regarding the matter.

“We told those of them who approached us to go back and begin their resignation processes from their wards then ensure that it is properly documented in accordance with the NNPP constitution.

“The Constitution of the NNPP (2023, as amended) contains provisions governing the resignation of members, while the Electoral Act, 2026 (as amended), regulates relevant aspects of political party membership, nomination and participation in elections.

” These provisions are not intended to be observed selectively or disregarded at the convenience of individual members, particularly persons who attained elective public office through the sponsorship, structures and electoral platform of the party.”

It pointed out that the letter to INEC would be updated to include some members elected on its platform in Katsina and Jigawa, who also did not complete their resignation processes.

“We are not scheming for any member to return but the right process must be followed to the letters. We believe in the rights of people to chose where they wish to belong but it must be properly documented as required by law.

“In the event of a post election lawsuit by their opponents requiring NNPP to come with records of their resignation, we will do so. As a party, the NNPP is firm on issues regarding its constitution and image and will not renage on that.

“We do not know the windows open to them now to complete their resignation but we will attend to those who wish to complete the process.

“The electoral guidelines, party constitution and the constitution of Nigeria are specific on the processes and procedures of resignation from a political party.

“We are all witnesses to the fact that elected officers of political parties have been in the abuse of processes and procedures to be followed when resigning from political parties.”

According to the party, what seems to be the norm is that some of the candidates claim that due to internal crisis in their previous political parties, they tendered resignation letter at their ward levels.

“Unfortunately most of them do not ensure that such resignation letters were documented and recorded at the national secretariat of the party and material evidence obtained.

“The national secretary has the mandate to keep the register of all members of each political party nationwide.

“Any member, who claims to have resigned from a political party and did not ensure that such records are documented and recorded at the national secretariat of the party and material evidence obtained, is deemed not to have resigned.

“It is even funny to note that some elected members of the national assembly openly resigned their membership of a political party during plenaries.Some don’t even bother to notify the parties on whose platform they were elected.

“This abuse of people’s mandate for selfish interest must be put to a stop. The consequences of their ungratefulness is that they never realised that they belong to two political parties, which is against the electoral laws and the Constitution of Nigeria, and should therefore, suffer the consequences.

“The only members exempted from the resignation saga are those who were expelled from the NNPP.

“NNPP secured victory at the Abia State High Court Uzuakoli, Federal Capital Territory High Court Abuja and Appeal Court in Owerri, to earn full recognition of INEC to restore the original logo and filled candidates for the 2027 general elections.

“Betrayers, who cannot provide INEC with a valid record of resignation are deemed members of NNPP, and cannot be candidates of any other political party for the purposes of contesting the 2027 general elections,” it added.

World.title: Tomato prices remain high as pepper gets cheaper in Lagos
World.content:
The drop in pepper prices has brought some relief to traders and buyers in Lagos markets, but the high cost of tomatoes continues to weigh on traders’ sales and consumers’ purchasing power.

Traders and consumers who spoke with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interview in Lagos described how changing prices had affected sales, household spending and the quantities of produce they could afford.

They cited seasonal availability and transportation costs among the factors influencing the market.

Malam Mohammed, a tomato seller at Costain Bus Stop, said he sourced his produce from Mile 12 Market, where prices varied according to variety, size and place of origin.

He said a paint of tomatoes, which sold for N6,000 in August and September, now cost N7,000, while a basket had risen from between N35,000 and N40,000 to between N45,000 and N65,000.

Mohammed explained that the high cost of tomatoes made it difficult for traders to maximise profits, adding that some customers complained about the sizes and quantities they received for the prices paid.

“This business is not a straight business,” he said.

He said the complaints had caused him to lose some customers, prompting him to reduce the quantity of tomatoes he purchased at a time to avoid losses from spoilage.

Mohammed also said a large bag of pepper currently sold for between N30,000 and N40,000, although he could not recall its exact price in August and September because of fluctuations.

Mrs Rukayat Sherif, another trader at Costain Bus Stop, said she bought tomatoes and pepper from Mile 12 Market because she trusted the source.

She said a basket of Ghana tomatoes currently sold for between N40,000 and N45,000, compared with N50,000 and above in August and September.

Sherif added that a paint of tomatoes now cost N7,000, against between N4,000 and N5,000 in September.

She said a small bag of pepper, which sold for between N30,000 and N35,000 in August and September, now cost between N20,000 and N25,000.

Sherif noted that five pieces of tomatoes sold for N500, while pepper was also available for N500 in small rubber plates containing a generous quantity.

She attributed the price changes partly to seasonal availability and transportation costs, explaining that some tomatoes damaged during transportation the previous week had been sold at reduced prices to prevent further deterioration.

She expressed hope that tomato prices would fall to more affordable levels, adding that lower prices would improve sales and reduce customers’ complaints.

Mrs Regina Owho, a tomato seller at Suru Market, Suru-Alaba, said large baskets of tomatoes currently sold for about N50,000, while smaller baskets cost between N35,000 and N45,000.

Owho recalled that a basket sold for about N40,000 in August and September, although prices fluctuated during that period.

She said the frequent changes made it difficult for traders to predict their purchasing costs, adding that the basket she bought on the day of the interview cost N40,000.

Mrs Mary Chigozie, a resident of Vaughan Street, Costain, said she spent between N2,000 and N5,000 daily on tomatoes and pepper but had reduced the quantities used in cooking because of the high cost of tomatoes.

She said small quantities of tomatoes that previously sold for N200 or N300 now cost N500 or N1,000.

Chigozie explained that she sometimes combined pepper with tomato paste or prepared red-oil stew when fresh tomatoes became too expensive.

She expressed concern that prices could rise further during the December festive period and urged the government to support and protect farmers.

On pepper, Mrs Rukayat Rasheeb, a trader at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, Costain, said a bag currently sold for between N45,000 and N60,000, the same price range recorded in August and September.

She, however, observed that pepper was now more plentiful than during the earlier period.

Rasheeb explained that prices generally declined when pepper was in season and increased when it became scarce.

She expressed optimism that prices could fall further, while noting that transportation and loading expenses added to traders’ costs.

Mr Okoro Ebubechi, who also sells pepper at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, said he currently bought a small basket for N20,000, compared with between N30,000 and N40,000 in September.

He attributed the reduction to increased availability during the current season, adding that transportation expenses influenced the prices charged by traders.

Ebubechi said customers were buying larger quantities because pepper had become more affordable.

He added that he sold pepper in different quantities, including portions worth N500, to accommodate buyers with varying budgets.

He expected prices to rise again in December if pepper became less available.

Mrs Odunayo Igwe, a pepper trader at Ilogbo Mosque, Apapa Road, said a bag currently sold for N30,000, the same price recorded in September.

She explained that although the price had remained unchanged, pepper was now more plentiful than in September, when supplies were lower.

Igwe also identified transportation costs as a factor affecting selling prices and expressed hope that prices would decline further.

Mrs Patience Niju, a pepper seller at Suru Market, Suru-Alaba, said she currently bought a small bag for N25,000 and a larger bag for N40,000.

She added that a small bag of shombo cost N20,000, while a larger one sold for N30,000.

Niju said the prices were unchanged from August and September, but the bags contained more pepper in October.

She welcomed the increased quantity, saying it encouraged customers to buy more and helped her sales move faster.

Mrs Teni David, a civil servant residing in Iyana Ipaja, said N200 to N500 could now buy more pepper than in August and September, when the same quantity cost between N1,000 and N1,500.

She said the increased availability had enabled her to buy larger quantities for household consumption.

David attributed the seasonal glut partly to limited preservation facilities, explaining that large quantities of pepper entered the market as the produce ripened, prompting traders to sell quickly before it lost its freshness.

She called on the government to establish more processing centres where farmers and traders could preserve and package pepper during periods of abundance.

According to her, such facilities would help reduce waste and maintain supplies during the off-season.

David warned that prices could rise again when the current season ended.

Ms Mary Udonwa, another pepper consumer, said the produce had become more affordable, allowing households to buy larger quantities.

She said she currently spent between N500 and N1,500 on pepper, depending on her needs.

Udonwa explained that high prices in August and September had forced her to reduce the amount used in cooking, sometimes relying on small quantities or ground pepper when fresh pepper became expensive.

She attributed the current reduction to increased market supply and suggested that some sellers might be lowering prices to avoid losses from spoilage.

Udonwa also expected pepper prices to rise during the Christmas and New Year festivities.

World.title: NDLEA recovers tons of illicit drug consignments in nine states
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has recovered tons of illicit drugs in Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta states.

The Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi, said this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja.

Giving a breakdown, Babafemi said a suspect was arrested in Warri, Delta with a huge cache of pharmaceutical opioids.

These included 29,350 capsules of tramadol, 6,620 tablets of tramadol 200mg, 4,116 bottles of codeine syrup, 11,340 tablets of Rohypnol and 3,500 tablets of diazepam.

“Others are 300 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 200 ampoules of diazepam injection, and quantities of tramadol 225mg, Molly and Cocodamol.

“He was transferred along with a white Hummer bus from the Nigeria Police Force, Delta State,” he said.

In a separate arrest at Enhere Junction, Warri, a 46-year-old physically challenged woman was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 with 6.0kg of skunk.

Meanwhile, a 41-year-old suspect was also arrested on Oct. 19 in Adamasingba, Ibadan, Oyo State, following his initial escape from arrest when NDLEA officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis sativa from his house on Sept. 16.

Babafemi said a raid in Gerawa area of Kano on Oct. 22 led to the arrest of a suspect and seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis sativa weighing 97.2kg.

Also, NDLEA officers at the Lankaviri checkpoint, Yorro Local Government Area, Taraba, on Oct. 23, arrested another suspect with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg.

“The same day, the Nigeria Police Force handed over a suspect arrested at Dakka village, Bali LGA, with 112 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 81.49kg,” he said.

Similarly, in Niger State, another suspect was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 on Sabo-Kainji road, Borgu LGA, with 64,000 pills of opioids, including tramadol and diazepam.

Babafemi said NDLEA officers also arrested another suspect on Oct. 21 at Nasaru Town, Ningi LGA, Bauchi State, where they seized 379kg of cannabis sativa packed in seven jumbo sacks.

“Acting on intelligence, NDLEA officers on Oct. 20 raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, Ondo, and recovered 56 bags of abandoned cannabis sativa weighing 583kg.

“Two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West LGA, Edo, with an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg, were destroyed on Oct. 18 by NDLEA operatives.

“They also burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took 97kg as exhibit,” he said.

In a related operation at Ewe community, Owan West, another suspect was arrested with 35kg of the same psychoactive substance.

With the same vigour, commands and formations of the agency across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation activities to schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities, among others, in the past week.

These include WADA enlightenment lectures to students and staff of Oje Grammar School, Ibadan, Oyo State; Government Day Secondary School, Kwamba, Niger State, Baptist Primary School, Olorunda, Ogun.

Others are Government Secondary School, Yalea, Kano State; Community Secondary School, Igogoro, Enugu State; Urban Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra; and Kelebe Community Grammar School, Osogbo, Osun, among others.

Babafemi quoted the NDLEA Chairman, retired Brig.-Gen. Buba Marwa, as commending the officers and men of Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta commands for their vigilance.

This, he said, included their diligence, professionalism and intelligence-driven approach to the various successful operations.

Marwa urged them and their colleagues across the country to sustain the tempo of the war against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

World.title: IGP Disu proposes 200% gratuity, pension for retired officers
World.content:
IGP Disu

The Inspector-General of Police (I-G), Mr Olatunji Disu, has proposed a 200 per cent gratuity and pension for retired police officers as part of the ongoing reforms in the Nigeria Police Force.

Disu told newsmen on Sunday in Abuja that the proposal was before a Presidential Committee, set up to examine police concerns and recommend sustainable solutions.

He said the proposal was to intensify efforts to secure improved retirement benefits for personnel of the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) and address the longstanding pension challenges.

The I-G also said that the committee was made up of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation.

According to him, other representative in the committee are the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, the Budget Office of the Federation and the National Pension Commission (PenCom).

“Under the proposed arrangement, eligible officers can retire on pension benefits linked to their last salaries, alongside the enhanced gratuity.”

Disu said the package was also, expected to address recurring protests by serving officers, seeking to exit the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), a contentious issue within the force.

“The initiative is aimed at resolving the outstanding pension liabilities, provide more adequate retirement benefits and create a more efficient pension administration system.

“It also seeks to cover officers who retired before the new framework takes effect, with provisions to review their benefits in line with the revised terms, rather than limiting reform to future retirees,” he said.

I-G said the intervention of President Bola Tinubu in the police pension crisis had raised expectations among retired officers, who had long complained about inadequate benefits, delayed payments and administrative bottlenecks.

According to him, for many pensioners, timely access to benefits is essential for meeting household expenses and medical bills amid rising living costs.

He said the Federal Government had cleared the backlog of pension payments that previously left some retirees waiting for up to two years and introduced pension increment.

Disu revealed that some of the beneficiaries currently receive almost double of their previous payments.

“Our engagement with the presidency, PenCom and other relevant institutions is seen as important to sustain the NPF reform momentum.

“The committee is expected to recommend measures on outstanding liabilities, funding arrangements and benefit administration.

“It is also, to provide a framework to resolve pension challenges and improve coordination among the institutions responsible for policy, funding and administration,” he said.

He added that the proposal remained subject to the committee’s deliberations, relevant government approvals, funding arrangements and implementation guidelines.

He said the 200 per cent gratuity should not be regarded as approved or existing entitlement, adding that the final outcome would determine whether it would be adopted.

World.title: Enugu Catholic Diocese Launches Initiative To Hold Public Officials Accountable
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has launched an initiative to promote good governance, civic engagement and voter education, while encouraging citizens to demand accountability and quality representation from elected officials.

The initiative, known as Church for Community Care and Good Governance (CCGG), was launched Sunday by the Catholic Institute for Development, Justice and Peace (CIDJAP).

Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, the Project Lead, Rev. Fr. Longinus Ugonwa, said the initiative would connect the church with citizens’ everyday concerns, including education, healthcare, roads, security, employment, youth development and responsible leadership.

He said CCGG was neither a political party nor a platform for promoting or attacking political personalities, but was committed to truth, responsible citizenship and the common good.

According to him, the initiative would help citizens understand public issues, ask informed questions, examine evidence and make responsible decisions rather than dictate what they should think.

“CCGG would also promote constructive engagement between citizens and political leaders,” he said, adding that governance worked better when citizens were informed and institutions remained open to dialogue.

He said the initiative would use podcasts, radio programmes, interviews, documentaries, social media and community engagement to listen to citizens, examine public concerns, recognise genuine progress and encourage practical solutions.

In his remarks, the Chairman of Enugu East Local Government Area, Beloved-Dan Anike, said the church could not separate itself from governance.

He expressed his readiness to partner with CCGG to achieve its objectives.

World.title: Nigeria Woos Korean Investors As Seoul Highlights Youth Initiatives
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Nigeria has urged South Korean companies to increase investment in manufacturing, agriculture, technology and shipbuilding, seeking to leverage Korea’s industrial expertise to boost local production, create jobs and accelerate economic growth.

The appeal was made by the Chief of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Babagana Wakil, who represented the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, at a reception to mark Korea’s National Day in Abuja, weekend.

Speaking on behalf of the minister, Wakil said Korea’s achievements in industrialisation, technology and infrastructure offered valuable lessons for Nigeria as it pursued economic diversification.

He urged Korean firms to explore opportunities in local manufacturing and assembly, shipbuilding and other industries capable of expanding Nigeria’s industrial base.

He said Nigeria was interested in Korean expertise in agricultural mechanisation, particularly rice production and processing, to improve productivity and support food security. Other priority areas included digital technology, infrastructure, education, technical training, maritime security and fisheries.

Wakil reaffirmed the Nigerian government’s appreciation for Korea’s contributions to the country’s economic growth and skills development, stressing the need to expand trade and investment for mutual benefit.

South Korean Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, highlighted initiatives supported by his country in youth entrepreneurship, education and agricultural employment, describing Nigeria’s young population as a major asset.

He disclosed that the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) broke ground in September on the Abuja Centre for Entrepreneurship.

The centre is expected to support hundreds of young entrepreneurs and start-ups in turning business ideas into viable enterprises.

Jeong also said Korea’s Smart School project, implemented with the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), had reached 8,000 children and trained more than 300 teachers and school leaders.

In agriculture, KOICA and the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) are implementing initiatives aimed at creating green jobs for young Nigerians. Approximately 2,000 Nigerian officials have also received training in Korea through KOICA programmes, he said.

“Our shared goal is simple: more opportunities for young people, stronger local businesses, and better lives for our people,” Jeong said.

The ambassador named Daewoo Engineering & Construction, LG, Samsung, Hyundai and Solpia among Korean companies operating in Nigeria’s energy, manufacturing, clean water and digital technology sectors.

He said the Korean Embassy, working with the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), would continue to promote investment, technology transfer and local employment.

Jeong said Korea respected Nigeria’s development priorities and sought to work with the country as an equal partner, adding that stronger commercial ties could create jobs, strengthen local businesses and generate shared prosperity.

Nigeria and South Korea established diplomatic relations in 1980, with ties spanning trade, investment, education and technical assistance.

Nigeria is seeking to build on those relations to attract more capital and expertise for industrial expansion and employment generation.

World.title: Top10 Magazine Names Umaru Kwairanga As Man of the Year 2026
World.content:
The Group Chairman, Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group), Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, has been named the Top10 Magazine’s Man of the Year 2026.

He emerged from among many other distinguished personalities in a multi-stage rigorous selection and screening process.

He succeeds the Chairman of Casiva Ltd, Alhaji Nasiru Haladu Danu, who was the magazine’s Man of the Year for 2025.

He joins a club of distinguished Nigerians who have won the crown since the inception of the award over 10 years ago, with the late Group Managing Director of Access Bank, Dr. Herbert Wigwe, as the pioneer winner of the award in 2016.

Also on the magazine’s roll of honour are the Chairman, Cosgrove Group (2020), Umar Abdullahi; Chairman of Peace Mass Transit (PMT) and Founder of Maduka University (2022), Chief Samuel Onyishi; former Chairman, Federal Inland Revenue Service, FIRS (2023), Muhammad Nami and Senator George Akume (2024), among others.

In a letter conveying Alhaji Kwairanga’s selection as the Man of the Year 2026, the Board of Editors of the Magazine said it was in recognition of his towering leadership as custodian of Nigeria’s capital market, his role in driving national economic development, his championship of corporate governance, transparency, integrity and influence that defined Nigeria’s economic narrative in 2026.

These, the givers of the award said, clearly stand him out as a man of excellence worthy of celebration, “hence the decision of our management to accord you this special recognition as the Top 10 Magazine’s Man of the Year 2026,” the letter said.

In a year marked by economic reforms, market volatility and renewed investor search for trust and transparency, Kwairanga stood tall as a symbol of stability, integrity and visionary leadership.

Under his watch, the Nigerian Exchange has emerged as one of Africa’s best performing markets, restoring investor confidence, attracting foreign inflows and providing capital for enterprise growth that creates jobs for millions of Nigerians.

As overseer of NGX Regulation, he has championed board accountability, shareholder protection, ESG compliance and global best practices, elevating Nigerian corporate governance to world standard.

His influence goes beyond the trading floor of Marina. He is a trusted counsel to regulators, a respected voice in the Presidency’s economic circle, a bridge between the private sector and government, and a mentor to a generation of investors and entrepreneurs who see in him the embodiment of ethical capitalism.

A man of unblemished integrity, quiet philanthropy and profound intellect, Kwairanga represents the best of Northern and Nigerian leadership – humble yet powerful, principled yet pragmatic, traditional yet globally minded. In a nation in search of role models who prove that one can be successful without cutting corners, powerful without being oppressive and wealthy without losing humanity, Kwairanga stands as a beacon.

“For his towering leadership as custodian of Nigeria’s capital market, his role in driving national economic development, his championship of corporate governance and transparency, his integrity and influence that defined Nigeria’s economic narrative in 2026, the Board and Management of the Top10 Magazine unanimously select Alh. (Dr.) Umaru Kwairanga as Man of the year 2026,” stated the publishers of the Top10 Magazine.

The Top10 Magazine is a monthly publication established over 10 years ago as a platform to celebrate excellence and people of excellence from all human endeavours.

The Top10 Man of the Year Award was also instituted the same year as an annual award by the magazine as the highest honour reserved annually for one distinguished Nigerian whose leadership, integrity, influence and national impact have defined the year.

This year’s recipient, Kwairanga, a man of untainted character and impeccable reputation, is renowned for his unwavering commitment to success. Kwairanga has 25 years’ cognate experience in the banking, pensions, investment, manufacturing and commercial sectors.

He has served previously as a council member of the Nigerian Stock Exchange and is currently a council member of the Institute of Directors of Nigeria; and an active director on the boards of many quoted/listed and unquoted companies including Ashaka Cement Plc where he served for over 10 years, first as a director and later as chairman of the Board.

He is currently the GMD/CEO of Finmal Finance Services Limited. He is a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers, Fellow of Certified Pension Institute Nigeria (2005) and Fellow of Institute of Directors of Nigeria. He is Chairman – Commerce, Trade and Investment subcommittee of Gombe State transition committee.

Kwairanga has a B.Sc (Hons) Business Administration (1991) and MBA (1995) both from University of Maiduguri and M.Sc. Finance & Governance from Liverpool John Moores University (2007).

Publisher/Editor-In-Chief of the Top10 Magazine, Mr. Tony Iji, said the award will be presented to Kwairanga at the Top10 Magazine’s Annual Excellence Awards night slated for November 22, 2026 which will be graced by the crème de la crème of the society.

To mark this high-profile event, the magazine is putting together a special award edition to celebrate him and other awardees. The edition which will comprehensively chronicle his achievements, leadership journey, and contribution to Nigeria’s capital market and the economy in general.

World.title: Tinubu: I’m Working to Eradicate Inherited Hunger and Poverty
World.content:
•Shettima: President has consistently supported northern political interests

•Blaming opponents for hunger shameless attempt to dodge responsibility, Atiku replies Tinubu

• ADC mocks APC campaign flag-off over empty seats, rented crowd, recycled promises

• Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off ‘political theatre’, says Makinde

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu yesterday flagged off his 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State, declaring that he was working to eradicate inherited hunger and poverty created by his political opponents when they were in power.

Tinubu, who spoke at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally, promised that his administration would create prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity.

This comes as Vice President Kashim Shettima declared that President Tinubu has consistently supported northern political interests, citing historical instances when the president provided vital political backing to major northern figures facing political adversity.

Meanwhile, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record.

Reacting to Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty, African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku described it as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery Tinubu’s government has inflicted on Nigerians.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has also described the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna as a monumental disappointment, accusing the ruling party of relying on rented crowds, empty seats and recycled promises.

Similarly, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has dismissed President Tinubu’s campaign flag-off as political theatre, accusing his administration of failing the North on security, economic welfare and political inclusion.

Speaking at yesterday’s campaign rally, Tinubu accused his political opponents of creating hunger and poverty, which his administration was tackling.

Tinubu stated: “I must thank you for your participation in the past elections. You gave me joy, and I will always remember the victory you gave me to become President. I have come again to thank you and seek your mandate for a second term to fulfill our promise of prosperity, continuity, progress and development.

“I hear my opponents talking about hunger. Who created it? They did. They created hunger and poverty. We are trying to eradicate them. We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working, and I am proud of them. They are developing their states.

“To you, the children of our country, we promise prosperity in our second term. You will not regret going to the polls.

“Do you have your PVC? This is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry… They have nothing to offer you but heckling. We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you of that.”

The president urged voters to vote for all the ruling party’s candidates during the election.

He noted: “Your prosperity is here. Your good fortune is in your hands. Your fingerprints will reflect this. Be careful. Watch them. Do not let them lie to you.

“What is past is past. Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies and no more smuggling.”

Shettima: Tinubu Had Consistently Supported Northern Political Interests

Also speaking at the rally, Vice President Shettima stated that President Tinubu had consistently supported northern political interests.

“And I want us to bear in mind and go back to the past. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased out of the PDP, with his tail between his legs, he ran to the land of the Jagaban, who gave him political succour, support, and a platform to contest the presidency in 2007.

“Again, in 2011, President Tinubu supported another Northern man, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, to contest for the presidency of this country. You can also see that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured his first- and second-term victories. This is why we have all stood with him. This is a mark of honour, and our faith in a man of honour.”

Shettima said Tinubu’s administration had also kept the country together despite predictions of failure and had delivered on key promises.

Shettima also cited several projects delivered by Tinubu’s administration.

Gov Sani Challenges Northern Candidates to Show Records

Kaduna State Governor Senator Sani challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record, stressing that Tinubu had fulfilled key campaign promises made to Kaduna State in 2022, particularly on road reconstruction and security in Birnin Gwari.

He recalled Tinubu’s visit to Birnin Gwari LGA on December 22, 2022, when the area was the epicentre of insecurity in the North-west.

Addressing the President, Sani said: “At that time, a very senior officer advised you against going to Birnin Gwari because of security concerns. You instantly rejected the advice and travelled to Birnin Gwari with 27 armoured vehicles.”

According to the governor, two promises made during that visit have been met, adding that the 123km Kaduna-Birnin Gwari Road abandoned for over 40 years was under reconstruction.

Sani said the government had released N117 billion to the contractor.

He noted: “Today you can travel to Birnin Gwari with your eyes closed without a single police escort. That is progress.”

The governor challenged opposition figures to show their track record.

“When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him, can you show us a track record?” Sani said.

Also, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, said the campaign would be based on records in the economy, infrastructure, health, education and cash transfers.

“We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country.”

He added: “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant.”

For his part, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, declared that Tinubu has earned the confidence and support of Nigerians through his courageous leadership, commitment to national development, and promise of greater prosperity for the country.

Blaming Opposition for Hunger Shameless Attempt to Dodge Responsibility, Atiku Replies Tinubu

Meanwhile, Atiku has described Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.

In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the former Vice President argued that a President cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record.

“The hardship your administration has brought upon Nigerians is real. You cannot deny it by blaming others.

“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” Atiku added.

ADC Mocks APC Campaign Flag-off Over Empty Seats, Rented Crowd, Recycled Promises

Reacting to the rally, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Mr. Kola Ologbondiyan, said an event intended to demonstrate the APC’s political strength across the North-west had instead exposed what he described as the party’s declining public acceptance.

Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC mobilised people from the seven states of the North-west and beyond, with payments reportedly ranging from N50,000 to N100,000 per person. Yet, the stadium, which he put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied.

He added that the turnout, which he described as disappointing, was compounded by what he called the unenthusiastic reception given to the speeches and messages of APC leaders.

Ologbondiyan further alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling party after leaving the stadium, chanting the Hausa phrase “Ba mu yi,” which he interpreted as a rejection of the APC and its policies.

The ADC-PCC accused the APC of returning to Kaduna with promises similar to those made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles, arguing that the ruling party had failed to account for its years in power adequately.

Tinubu’s Kaduna Campaign Flag-off ‘Political Theatre’, Says Makinde

On its part, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) said the APC campaign event would not erase what it described as broken promises, worsening hardship and declining public confidence in the ruling party.

In a statement issued by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, MDPCO challenged Tinubu to explain what the North had gained from his administration beyond persistent insecurity, economic difficulties and what it called marginalisation.

MDPCO alleged that at least 20,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while millions had been displaced by insecurity. The statement did not independently verify the figures.

The organisation further alleged that the North had been marginalised in appointments to strategic federal positions, accusing the APC of treating the region primarily as a source of electoral support.

“No part of the country should be an electoral warehouse to be raided every four years and abandoned after victory,” the group said.

World.title: NDC Fixes Monday for Third NEC Meeting, Presidential Campaign Council Unveiling
World.content:
•Says 80% of candidates received free nomination forms amid economic hardship

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) will unveil its National Campaign Council on Monday as part of preparations for the 2027 general election, while presenting its financial accounts to demonstrate its commitment to transparency and accountability.

The party disclosed this in a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, announcing that its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting would be held at 10 a.m. on October 26 at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, Maitama, Abuja.

A major highlight of the meeting, according to the party, will be the National Treasurer’s presentation of the party’s statement of account, a move it said is intended to distinguish its financial management practices from those of other political parties.

The NDC challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures to promote transparency in managing party finances.

The party also attributed its financial limitations partly to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, claiming that approximately 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the fees for expression-of-interest forms.

It said it had consequently issued the forms to the affected candidates free of charge to enable them to participate in the electoral process.

The party blamed the situation on what it described as widespread poverty, hunger and deprivation under the APC-led federal government, criticising its economic policies.

Beyond the financial disclosures, the NEC meeting will give the party an opportunity to unveil its National Campaign Council, which it said would coordinate its campaign activities across all levels of government.

According to the statement, the council will encompass the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly campaign structures.

The party also announced plans to present certificates of return to its candidates contesting the various elective positions.

The developments come as political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general election, with campaign structures, candidate mobilisation and party organisation expected to play important roles in the contest.

For the NDC, the planned unveiling of its campaign council and disclosure of its accounts are intended to project organisational readiness and distinguish the party’s approach to internal financial accountability.

The NDC expressed confidence in its preparations for the forthcoming elections, saying it was determined to offer Nigerians what it described as altruistic leadership.

The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. The time is 10 am prompt.

“A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This reflects our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in managing their finances.

“For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.

“Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge.

“The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC).

“As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils.

“Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices.

“The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!”

World.title: Crude Oil Price Surges Above $117 Over Fears of Fresh US Strikes on Iran
World.content:
• Oil theft slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in five years amid fresh uptick in losses

• Navy uncovers 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Bonny

Emmanuel Addeh and Linus Aleke in Abuja

Crude oil prices surged above $117 a barrel at the weekend, reaching their highest level since April, as fears of renewed US military strikes on Iran and escalating threats to energy infrastructure across the Middle East heightened concerns about global crude supplies.

This comes as oil theft and pipeline losses in Nigeria fell by 82.9 per cent in five years, from 102,900 barrels per day (bpd) in 2021 to 17,600 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, amid fresh concerns about further increases in lost volumes after years of decline.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny Local Government Area (LGA) of Rivers State, disrupting a potential storage point in the illicit petroleum supply chain as troops of Operation Delta Sentinel intensified their clampdown on oil theft and economic saboteurs in the Niger Delta region.

Nigeria’s oil benchmark, Brent crude, climbed by about 3.5 per cent to cross $117 a barrel during trading before easing to just above $116, still up approximately 2.7 per cent.

The latest rally followed reports that Washington was considering fresh military strikes against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, raising concerns that the conflict, now in its eighth month, could escalate further rather than move towards a diplomatic resolution.

Iran had threatened to attack oil facilities, undersea cables, data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure across the Gulf if the United States and Israel launched a new offensive against the country.

Brent crude traded at about $72 a barrel in February, before the war began, but surged to about $126 a barrel by the end of April as the conflict intensified and concerns mounted over supply security.

Tensions rose again during the week following claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) that it struck four commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday.

The US ordered some diplomats and family members of American government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which had faced continued attacks by Houthi rebels operating from Yemen.

World.title: Oil Theft Slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in Five Years Amid Fresh Uptick in Losses
World.content:
Meanwhile, official operational statistics published by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed that daily crude oil losses, which fell to a five-year low of 9,100 bpd in 2025, rose by 93.4 per cent to 17,600 bpd between January and July 2026.

The figures in the commission’s fifth anniversary publication, ‘The Upstream Gaze’, highlighted both progress in curbing crude theft and the ongoing challenge of protecting oil production and transportation infrastructure.

According to the data, daily losses declined from 102,900 bpd in 2021 to 55,000 bpd in 2022, representing a 46.5 per cent reduction. The downward trend continued in 2023 when losses dropped to 22,900 bpd, before falling further to 11,200 bpd in 2024 and 9,100 bpd in 2025.

The federal government attributed the cut in crude losses to the combined efforts of the military, local pipeline surveillance groups in the Niger Delta, and the introduction of modern crude measuring devices in the region.

The figures showed that Nigeria’s total liquid hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil and condensate, gradually recovered from the lows recorded in recent years.

Output averaged 1.63 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 1.62 million bpd in 2025, 1.56 million bpd in 2024, 1.47 million bpd in 2023 and 1.38 million bpd in 2022. Production stood at 1.62 million bpd in 2021, the NUPRC data highlighted.

Crude oil production alone averaged 1.46 million bpd in the period under review, up from 1.43 million bpd in 2025, 1.35 million bpd in 2024, 1.24 million bpd in 2023 and 1.14 million bpd in 2022. The figure for 2021 was 1.31 million bpd.

In contrast, blended condensate production continued its downward trend, averaging 170,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 190,000 bpd in 2025, 210,000 bpd in 2024, 230,000 bpd in 2023, 240,000 bpd in 2022, and 310,000 bpd in 2021.

The gradual improvement in crude production also coincided with a significant shift in how the country allocates its oil, particularly the growing share supplied to domestic refineries as Nigeria expands its local refining capacity.

Supply to domestic refineries climbed to 460,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, up from 280,000 bpd in 2025, 220,000 bpd in 2024, 20,000 bpd in 2023, and just 10,000 bpd in 2022. Domestic refinery supply was virtually non-existent in 2021.

At 460,000 bpd, local refineries accounted for approximately 29 per cent of the 1.61 million bpd in total crude oil lifted during the period. The allocation represented a 64.3 per cent increase over the 280,000 bpd supplied to domestic refineries in 2025, underscoring growing demand for locally processed crude.

Similarly, the shift coincided with a decline in crude available for export, as the government struggled to meet local supply. Average daily crude exports fell to 1.15 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, from 1.33 million bpd in 2025; 1.31 million bpd in 2024; 1.47 million bpd in 2023; 1.32 million bpd in 2022 and 1.51 million bpd in 2021.

The latest export figures were down 13.5 per cent from the 2025 level and 23.8 per cent from the 2021 volume.

In the same vein, total crude lifting averaged 1.61 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, marginally below the 1.62 million bpd recorded in 2025. The figures suggested that the growing allocation to domestic refineries has been accompanied by a reduction in export volumes, rather than a comparable increase in total crude lifted.

World.title: Navy Uncovers 132,000 litres of Stolen Crude Oil in Bonny
World.content:
Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny LGA of Rivers State.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the Forward Operating Base Bonny discovered the stolen crude oil under Operation Delta Sentinel, following actionable intelligence.

He said the operation uncovered 10 dugout pits, adding that the site and the recovered products were handled in accordance with extant regulations.

“The operation reinforces the importance of intelligence-led action in identifying concealed petroleum stockpiles and disrupting the infrastructure that enables crude oil theft and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products.

“The Nigerian Navy will sustain efforts to locate and dismantle illegal refining infrastructure and disrupt the networks facilitating crude oil theft across the Niger Delta,” the statement said.

The Navy urged community leaders, residents, traditional institutions and other stakeholders to promptly report crude oil theft, illegal refining, suspicious petroleum storage and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products to the nearest security agency.

Timely, credible information, the statement said, could enable swift intervention and prevent illicit activities from expanding.

“Safeguarding the nation’s critical petroleum assets requires vigilance and active cooperation between security agencies and the communities they serve. The Navy therefore urges the public to remain alert and support lawful efforts to protect national resources,” Folorunsho concluded.

World.title: The best Kruger rest camps for a first-time safari
World.content:
Choosing where to stay can make a big difference to a first visit to the Kruger National Park, particularly for travellers planning to explore the park in their own vehicle.

The park has 12 main rest camps, along with smaller satellite and bushveld camps. The main camps are generally the easiest starting point for first-time visitors, as they offer facilities such as shops, restaurants, fuel stations and communal braai areas.

SANParks provides an overview of the available Kruger rest camps and facilities. Take a look.



1. Skukuza Rest Camp

Best for: First-time visitors who want plenty of facilities

Skukuza is Kruger’s largest rest camp and administrative headquarters. Situated beside the Sabie River in the southern part of the park, it offers a broad range of accommodation and facilities, making it a convenient base for visitors who want to combine game drives with a comfortable stay.

The camp has a restaurant, shop, fuel station and other amenities, while its location gives visitors access to a network of game-viewing roads in the wildlife-rich south. SANParks lists Skukuza among the park’s main accommodation options.

Its size and popularity mean it can feel busy, especially during peak holiday periods. However, for first-timers who want convenience and a wide choice of services, it is a practical option.

2. Lower Sabie Rest Camp

Best for: River views and game viewing

Lower Sabie is another popular option in southern Kruger. The camp overlooks the Sabie River, one of the park’s perennial rivers, and offers views towards the Lebombo Mountains.



Its setting is a major drawcard, but the surrounding area is also known for game viewing. Visitors can explore nearby roads and river routes in search of elephants, buffalo, antelope and predators.

The camp caters to different budgets and travel styles, with accommodation options ranging from camping to self-catering units. It also has facilities for visitors who prefer not to prepare every meal themselves.

Lower Sabie is a good choice for travellers who want to spend much of their time on game drives but still return to a scenic camp at the end of the day.

3. Satara Rest Camp

Best for: Visitors hoping to see lions and other big cats

Satara is located in central Kruger, in an area known for its open savannah and strong game-viewing opportunities.

SANParks describes the camp as being in one of the park’s better game-viewing areas, with lion, leopard and cheetah recorded regularly. Elephants, buffalo, giraffes, zebras and other general game are also found in the surrounding area.

The rest camp has a more rustic feel than some larger accommodation hubs, while still offering the main facilities visitors need for a self-drive stay.

Satara is particularly worth considering if seeing predators is high on your safari wish list. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed, however, and the animals move freely throughout the park.

4. Berg-en-Dal Rest Camp
