Best for: A scenic southern base

Berg-en-Dal lies in the south-western part of Kruger, beside the Matjulu Spruit. Unlike the flatter landscapes associated with some other parts of the park, this area has a more rugged, hilly setting.

The camp offers a range of accommodation, as well as facilities including a shop, restaurant, fuel station and swimming pool. It can suit visitors who want the convenience of a main rest camp while exploring a different landscape in the southern section of Kruger.

It is also worth considering for travellers entering through the park’s southern gates, depending on their route and itinerary.

5. Letaba Rest Camp

Best for: A quieter-feeling base in central Kruger

Letaba sits on a bend of the Letaba River, roughly midway between the park’s northern and southern boundaries. Its river setting and surrounding vegetation make it a scenic alternative to the busier southern camps.

SANParks notes that the sandy riverbed near Letaba is a good place to look for wildlife, particularly elephants. The camp also has facilities that make it a practical overnight stop, including a restaurant, shop and fuel station.

For first-time visitors planning a longer trip, Letaba can also be part of an itinerary that explores more than just the southern section of the park.

So, which Kruger camp should you choose?

If you want… Consider… A convenient all-round base Skukuza River views and southern game viewing Lower Sabie A focus on big cats Satara A scenic setting in southern Kruger Berg-en-Dal To explore further north of the main southern circuit Letaba

For a first visit, it is often easier to choose one main camp and explore the surrounding roads rather than spend every night moving between different camps. Kruger is a large park, and driving distances can take longer than expected when wildlife sightings and stops are part of the plan.

If you have several nights, consider splitting your stay between the south and central Kruger to experience different habitats. Book as early as possible for school holidays and other busy travel periods, and check the official SANParks accommodation and booking pages for available units, current rates and facilities.

Finally, remember that no camp can guarantee sightings of a particular animal. Give yourself time, set out early when possible and enjoy the smaller sightings along the way, too.

World.title: SRD grant a “material risk” to government, declares Treasury
World.content:
Does National Treasury have money to make the SRD grant permanent? Image: Wikimedia Commons

On Wednesday, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced that the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant would be extended for another 5 months.

While this plan was partially celebrated, it also gives the government time to work on a long-term solution.

This plan may include efforts to prevent the grant from bankrupting National Treasury.



Does the government have money for the SRD grant?

The Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant was one of three risks the government highlighted in its Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS).

In the section highlighting fiscal risks, National Treasury explained that the “legal challenges” surrounding the grant meant it was a risk to the country’s expenditure.

The section references the January 2025 High Court ruling declaring parts of the grant, including the means test threshold, invalid.



Now, Treasury awaits a decision by the Supreme Court of Appeal, which heard the case in August 2026.

If the SCA upholds the High Court ruling, Treasury suggests “beneficiary numbers and the total cost of the grant could increase substantially.”

Treasury suggests that this would double spending on the grant.



The decision would increase the grant’s annual funding requirement from R36 billion to R74 billion.

However, Treasury estimates it would only add 3 million beneficiaries to the current 13 million eligible for the SRD grant.

Tight-fisted Treasury Running Out of Room

In January 2025, the state argued that because the grant was temporary, it didn’t need to meet the provisions of the Social Assistance Act.



The High Court disagreed.

In that case, the state admitted it only budgeted for 10.5 million beneficiaries to receive the grant.

According to the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) June 2026 report, 7.9 million people receive the grant.



At the time of the report, only 89% had been paid out.

This suggests the government is actively pursuing its 10.5 million cap, despite 18 million applicants.

By extending the SRD grant in its current form until 31 March 2027, Treasury also has the opportunity to reshape the grant based on the SCA ruling.



In the 2026 National Budget, Treasury budgeted R36.9 billion for the SRD grant.

But the budget also reveals that Treasury only allocated R1.72 billion for the grant in 2027.

The MTBPS confirms this.

In changes to the budget’s non-interest expenditure, Treasury reduces spending on the SRD grant by R6.7 billion over the next 2 years.

World.title: The animals you can see at Addo Elephant National Park
World.content:
Addo Elephant National Park is home to more than just elephants. Image: Flickr

Addo Elephant National Park is best known for its elephants (I mean, it’s in the name), but the Eastern Cape reserve is home to a huge variety of wildlife.

SANParks records 91 mammal species and 418 bird species in the park, including the Big Five.

Here’s what you could see on a safari.

The Big Five

African elephant

Elephants are Addo’s biggest attraction, with more than 600 elephants in the park. They can be seen throughout the main game-viewing area, with waterholes particularly useful on hot days.



Lion

Lions were reintroduced to Addo in 2003. They can be more difficult to find than elephants, however, as they spend much of their time resting or hidden in vegetation. SANParks says early morning and evening are among the better times to look for them.

Cape buffalo

Addo Elephant National Park is home to more than 400 Cape buffalo, according to SANParks. The park describes this as one of the largest disease-free buffalo herds in South Africa.

Black rhino

Black rhinos are also found in Addo, although they are considerably less predictable to spot than elephants and buffalo. A rhino sighting should therefore be considered a lucky one rather than a guaranteed part of your safari.



Leopard

Leopards do occur in Addo but are rarely seen. SANParks describes them as shy and secretive, making them one of the park’s more difficult Big Five sightings.

Other animals to look out for

The Big Five aren’t the only animals you’ll encounter. Addo is also home to:

Zebra

Kudu

Eland

Red hartebeest

Warthog

Spotted hyena

Bushbuck

Bushpig

Springbok

Gemsbok

SANParks describes species such as zebra, kudu, red hartebeest, eland and warthog as among the animals commonly found in the main game-viewing area. Spotted hyenas were reintroduced to the park in 2003 and are another predator visitors can look out for.



If you’re lucky, you could also spot some of the park’s more elusive species, including:

Aardwolf

Aardvark

Caracal

Meerkat

Honey badger

Bat-eared fox

Cape porcupine

Klipspringer

These are much harder to find, and many are nocturnal or particularly secretive.

Don’t overlook the dung beetles

One of Addo’s smallest residents is also one of its most famous. The park is home to the flightless dung beetle, which plays an important role in recycling nutrients in the ecosystem.



Drivers are asked to take care when travelling on the park’s roads because the beetles can be found crossing them.

What is Addo elephant national park’s Big 7?

Addo is also unusual because it is promoted as a Big 7 destination. Along with the traditional Big Five (Lion, Leopard, Elephant, Rhino and Buffalo), the wider park includes Southern right whales and Great white sharks.

These two marine species form part of Addo’s broader conservation area and are not animals you’ll see while driving around the main game-viewing section.



Which animals are easiest to see at Addo Elephant National Park?

While there are no guarantees on safari, some species are considerably easier to spot than others.

Animal How likely are you to see it? Elephant Very good Zebra Good Warthog Good Kudu Good Buffalo Good Lion Possible Spotted hyena Possible Rhino Possible Leopard Rare Aardvark/Aardwolf Rare

For the best chance of seeing wildlife, slow down and spend time around waterholes rather than simply trying to cover as many kilometres as possible.

SANParks allows visitors to explore the main game-viewing area in their own vehicles, making Addo a particularly accessible option for a self-drive safari.



And while elephants may be the animals you’re most likely to remember, spotting one of Addo’s elusive predators can make an already memorable safari even better.

World.title: Eskom confirms nine-hour power outage in parts of Gauteng on Thursday
World.content:
Eskom has announced a nine-hour power outage in Braamfischer, Soweto, on Thursday, 29 October.

The power utility confirmed the interruption in its Gauteng Cluster Connect bulletin for October 2026. Eskom says crews need to switch off supply to carry out essential maintenance on its distribution power lines.

The outage will affect customers in Braamfischer, and Eskom has urged residents to prepare ahead of the shutdown.



When the power outage will take place

Eskom will cut electricity supply in Braamfischer at 9:00 on Thursday, 29 October. The utility expects to restore power by 18:00 the same day.

Residents should charge cellphones, laptops and backup batteries the night before. Households should also plan meals and refrigeration, as the outage covers most of the day.

The utility warned that the planned maintenance may not go ahead as communicated if circumstances beyond its control arise. Residents should keep an eye on Eskom’s channels for any last-minute changes.

Eskom’s safety warning to Soweto residents

Eskom has advised customers to treat all electrical appliances as live at all times during the outage. Power could return without warning, so residents should not attempt repairs or tamper with wiring while supply is off.

Switching off appliances and unplugging sensitive electronics can also help protect them from power surges when electricity comes back on.

The utility thanked customers for their cooperation and apologised for any inconvenience the maintenance may cause.



Residents with questions or problems during the outage can reach through several channels.

Customers can download the self-help MyEskom Customer app or send a WhatsApp message to 0860037566. The USSD service is available by dialling *120*37566#.

For supply-related enquiries, customers can call Eskom’s Contact Centre on 08600 37566, which operates 24 hours a day. Bill-related enquiries can be checked online at csonline-Eskom.co.za from Monday to Friday, between 8:00 and 16:00.

World.title: The best self-drive routes in Addo Elephant National Park
World.content:
From Hapoor to Zuurkop, these Addo self-drive routes can help you make the most of your time in the national park. Image: Flickr

One of the biggest advantages of visiting Addo Elephant National Park is that you don’t need to book an expensive guided safari to experience its wildlife.

Visitors can explore the park’s tourist roads in their own vehicles, with both tarred and gravel roads available in the main game-viewing area.

In fact, SANParks says all tourist roads are accessible to normal cars, although some gravel roads may close during particularly wet weather. The speed limit is 40km/h, but visitors are advised to travel at around 20–30km/h for the best game-viewing experience.



But with a network of loops, waterholes, dams and viewpoints, it helps to have an idea of where you want to go before setting off.

Here are some of the best routes and areas worth considering on a self-drive safari.

1. The Matyholweni–Main Camp route

If you’re entering Addo Elephant National Park from the Matyholweni Gate near Colchester, you can turn your journey into a game drive by taking the southern access road through the park to Main Camp.



SANParks puts the distance between Matyholweni and Main Camp at about 39km, with the journey taking roughly two hours, depending on stops and your speed while game viewing.

This is considerably slower than driving around the park, but that’s exactly the point. Instead of simply travelling to your accommodation, you’re already on a wildlife-viewing route.

Keep your eyes open for elephants, buffalo, zebra, warthog and antelope along the way.



The route is not suitable for cars towing caravans or trailers or for buses, so visitors with those vehicles need to use another entrance route.

2. The Hapoor waterhole area

For elephant lovers, the area around Hapoor waterhole should be high on the list. SANParks specifically recommends waterholes for elephant viewing, particularly on hot days.

The park’s tourist road map includes the Hapoor Dam and surrounding roads, making this an obvious area to explore when you’re looking for Addo’s famous elephants.



Don’t simply drive past a waterhole because there aren’t animals there immediately. Game viewing is about patience, and spending 10 or 15 minutes watching a waterhole can sometimes produce a much better sighting than covering another few kilometres.

3. The Zuurkop and Ndlondo area

Another section worth exploring around the main game-viewing area is the Zuurkop/Ndlondo section.

The tourist-road map includes the Ndlondo Loop and Zuurkop Lookout, along with several surrounding routes and waterholes.



A lookout point also gives you a chance to get out of the vehicle safely and stretch your legs while taking in the landscape. This is a good area to include when you have several hours rather than simply trying to drive from one gate to another.

4. The Gorah and Ngulube area

The Gorah Loop and Ngulube Loop are another option for visitors wanting to explore more of the main game area.

The park map shows both routes, along with Ngulube Waterhole, and the wider network connects with other game-viewing roads. This is the type of route where it’s worth slowing down rather than trying to cover as much ground as possible.



Addo Elephant National Park’s main game area is home to the Big Five, while also supporting species including red hartebeest, eland, kudu, zebra, warthog and spotted hyena.

5. The Marion Baree and Spekboom area

The roads around Marion Baree Waterhole and Spekboom are another option to add to a longer self-drive.

The park’s tourist map shows Marion Baree Waterhole, Spekboom Hide and Spekboom Tented Camp in this part of the game-viewing area.



The Spekboom area is also useful for visitors staying at the tented camp, although there is an important restriction: guests staying at Spekboom cannot join the sunrise, sunset or night drives departing from Main Camp because the game-area gates are closed.

6. The Vukani and Mbotyi loops

If you’ve already covered some of the more central roads, the Vukani and Mbotyi loops provide further options for exploring the main game-viewing area.

Both are shown on SANParks’ current tourist-road map, alongside other loops and waterholes. The advantage of having several loops is that you don’t need to follow exactly the same road on every game drive.



Try one section in the morning and return via another route later in the day.

How long should you spend driving?

This depends on whether you’re trying to get somewhere or see animals.

If you’re simply travelling from Matyholweni to Main Camp, allow around two hours for the 39km route through the park. But for a proper self-drive safari, it’s worth allowing at least half a day.



But remember that Addo Elephant National Park is not a race. SANParks recommends driving at around 20–30km/h for maximum game-viewing enjoyment, despite the 40km/h maximum speed limit.

When is the best time to drive?

Early morning and late afternoon are particularly useful times for wildlife viewing.

SANParks notes that lions and spotted hyenas are most often seen in the early morning or evening to night-time, while hot days can be particularly good for elephant sightings around waterholes.



You also need to plan your route around the park’s gate hours.

SANParks’ current information lists game-area access at 05:30–18:30 during the summer months and generally 06:00–18:00 during winter. Visitors are not allowed to drive around the game area after the specified gate hours.

That means you shouldn’t start a long self-drive late in the afternoon without checking how much time you have left.

World.title: Tshwane mayoral candidates: Who wants to lead South Africa’s capital?
World.content:
Here are some of the mayoral candidates for the City of Tshwane. Images: X/Nasiphi Moya, Cilliers Brink, Omphile Maotwe, MK Party and VF Plus

Residents of the City of Tshwane will have several mayoral candidates to consider when they head to the polls on 4 November, with political parties putting forward current and former leaders to contest control of South Africa’s administrative capital.

The contest includes candidates from the Democratic Alliance (DA), ActionSA, the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party, the Freedom Front Plus (FF+) and the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP). The African National Congress (ANC), meanwhile, has said that it will only announce mayoral candidates after the elections.

The Democratic Alliance has nominated former Tshwane mayor Cilliers Brink, who is seeking to return to office after being removed through a motion of no confidence in September 2024.



Rand Water crisis affecting Tshwane consumers



Here is what we’ve been able to verify about the water outages in the east and the Moot areas of Pretoria. I stress that I am not the Mayor, but the Mayor isn’t communicating. Neither is the City.



On Sunday, a major inlet pipe burst… pic.twitter.com/OGYedxUaHf — Cilliers Brink (@CilliersB) October 24, 2026

Brink’s removal paved the way for ActionSA’s Dr Nasiphi Moya to become mayor in October 2024. Moya is now seeking to retain the position as ActionSA’s mayoral candidate.

Today, I spent some time in Region 7 – in areas that have been impacted by the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant crisis.



We are determined to ensure that all households in the area have access to water through water tankers, Jojo tanks and boreholes. This is a temporary… pic.twitter.com/d8ZJJ60d4v — Dr Nasiphi Moya (@nasiphim) October 24, 2026

The EFF has selected its treasurer-general, Omphile Maotwe, to contest the mayoral position. The party is also seeking to strengthen its presence in the municipality as voters prepare to elect a new city council.

Have yourself an Afrikaner who looks at you like Willie Spies 🤣🤣🤣 Don’t remind Donald Trump that bad things are happening in South Africa #VoteEFF pic.twitter.com/BT77EXImsv — Omphile Maotwe (@OmphileMaotwe) October 7, 2026

The MK Party has put forward Nkele Annie Matime.



LGE 2026 | MK Party mayoral candidate Nkele Annie Matime says the party will fight for land and mineral rights for residents of the City of Tshwane. pic.twitter.com/kxoiLpvkc2 — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 13, 2026

The Freedom Front Plus has nominated Willie Spies.

LGE 2026 | FF Plus mayoral candidate Willie Spies says property rights must be protected. pic.twitter.com/VcuGVA95hE — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 13, 2026

The IFP’s mayoral candidate is Douglas Ziyanda Zwane.

Mr. Douglas Ziyanda Zwane from South Africa shares the importance of increasing green cover during times of urbanisation. #U20Ahmedabad #G20India #U20MayoralSummit pic.twitter.com/Mm3SJjp9Ad — U20 INDIA (@U20India) July 8, 2023

The ANC had identified six potential candidates during its selection process: Aaron Maluleka, Kgoši Maepa, Chana Pilane-Majake, Tlangi Mogale, Patience Moropa and Phumeza Mangcu. However, the party had not publicly confirmed its final choice as mentioned above.

COALITION POLITICS IN THE SPOTLIGHT

Tshwane has experienced changes in political leadership and coalition arrangements since the 2021 local government elections, reflecting the challenges of governing a municipality where parties must negotiate to secure support in council.

The 2021 elections resulted in a fragmented council, with no single party securing an outright majority. Subsequent political disagreements and changes in support contributed to shifts in the mayoral leadership.

The 2026 election will determine the composition of the new city council, which will elect the mayor. Consequently, being nominated as a party’s mayoral candidate does not guarantee that a person will assume office.

Key issues for the next administration include municipal finances, reliable water and electricity supplies, infrastructure maintenance, service delivery and accountability.

World.title: Could Manqoba Mngqithi replace Fernando Cruz at Chiefs?
World.content:
Manqoba Mngqithi has been shown the door by Young Africans but will he end up joining Soweto giants Kaizer Chiefs?

The 55-year-old was linked to the Amakhosi job several times during his tenure at Mamelodi Sundowns.

On Saturday, Yanga sacked the former Golden Arrows, leaving him back in the market.



Chiefs have Fernando Da Cruz as head coach but his future will depend on how he turns the corner at the club. On Friday, he watched his team crash out of the CAF Confederation Cup in the preliminary stages.

Amakhosi sporting director Kaizer Motaung Jr assured that the coach’s job is safe.

“As a Club, we would like to reaffirm our full support for, and confidence in, the Head Coach and the entire technical team,” the statement read.

“They continue to have our trust as they lead the implementation of a football philosophy and development pathway that we firmly believe will bring sustainable success.

Mngqithi could still join Chiefs

“Their professionalism, work ethic, and commitment to improving the team every day remain irreproachable,” Chiefs said.

“The team is fighting hard every game to uphold a high standard of performance, and yesterday, despite the result and the injuries we carry, that warrior spirit was visible on the field.”



If Da Cruz fails to beat TS Galaxy in the Carling Knockout Cup and then losses the Soweto Derby against Orlando Pirates, Chiefs might pull the plug and open the door for Mngqithi.

Should Chiefs sack Da Cruz or keep him until the end of the season?

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: Warning bells
World.content:
The Sunday, 25 October episode of Carte Blanche investigates a disturbing case involving a teenager allegedly obsessed with school shootings, a dark online network where violent fantasies were reportedly encouraged and shared, and a brutal attack on a six-year-old girl.

The investigation explores how group chats, teenage relationships and disturbing fixations allegedly intersected in a hidden digital world where violence was glorified.

It also raises critical questions about whether the attack could have been prevented if warning signs had been recognised and acted upon, examining the online interactions and concerning behaviour that may have preceded the shocking incident.



Credibility among South African viewers

Carte Blanche is a South African investigative journalism television series that airs on M-Net every Sunday at 19:00.

Its first episode aired on 21 August 1988 and over the last 34-plus years has earned credibility among South African viewers for its investigation into corruption, consumer issues, and current events.
