World.title: DA faces tough fight in eThekwini
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The DA is targeting a stronger showing in eThekwini in the local government elections.

The party faces stiff competition from the MK Party, while the ANC is hoping to reclaim lost ground in the metro.

eNCA elections analyst Wayne Sussman said the DA will need to mobilise its support base and ensure voters turn out in large numbers.

"The areas like Chatsworth and Phoenix, where a lot of Indian voters live, they just be far more competitive. Over the last few elections, the DA has really consolidated that support and they haven’t got that many suburban competitors.

"The question is, can they motivate their voters to go out and vote? Because in 2024 there was a lot of excitement about Chris Papas, but the excitement amongst DA support for Chris Papas paled into comparison for the excitement for Jacob Zuma. The DA’s differential turnout didn’t really pay dividends. However, they will be happy with these numbers. And it would be interesting to see how close they can finish to uMkhonto we-Sizwe.”

World.title: 'We are confident of a victory'  - Ramaphosa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC is confident it can win the Johannesburg metro outright in the upcoming local government elections.

ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa believes the party will have plenty to celebrate after the polls.

" An outright majority in the metro. That is a given. That is going to happen, and we have been attending to our own internal challenges and problems, streamlining the workings of our structures and making sure that there is greater commitment amongst our comrades.

"We are confident of a victory. You wait and see. There's going to be a lot of celebrations after the 4th of November," he said.

World.title: Johannesburg to host 2026 Whistleblowers Awards
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Whistleblowers Awards 2026 will be held in Johannesburg on Monday to recognise people who expose corruption and wrongdoing in the public and private sectors.

Public Interest SA's Tebogo Khaas said whistleblowers' role in exposing alleged wrongdoing and the risks they face when doing so has been highlighted at various commissions of inquiry.

"In darkness, democracy dies. And our mantra is let's make our democracy work. It is important that those who see wrongdoing being perpetrated, either in the private or public sector, they actually get to shine a light on it.

And in so doing, it will stem the tide of corruption, it will ensure that we encourage ethical leadership, but more importantly, ethical citizenship. And this year, we've seen the relevance or the importance of whistleblowing, as we've seen what the revelations before the Madanga Commission, and even going back to the Zondo Commission, where whistleblowers came and expressed what they saw and what they did about it. Unfortunately, in most instances, there's obviously retaliation and all that, but it is still important for people to speak out.

Should people speak out at all costs? No, we don't say that. It has to be done responsibly, but also in a manner that you also secure, you make sure that you don't put yourself at risk or others at risk."

World.title: ANC wants to secure Soweto votes
World.content:
SOWETO - The ANC said it's focusing on Soweto after poor voter turnout in the past two elections.

The party said Cyril Ramaphosa’s visit intends to mobilise residents to come out in their numbers and vote for the party.

Chief Whip Mdumiseni Ntuli said strong support in the area is key to the party's performance in the upcoming elections.

"Soweto, in the past two elections, we have not done well in terms of the attendance. Not that there was any other political party which did better than us, but knowing that this is our historical base, we decided that the president will have to spend more time here.

"You might have noticed that maybe he's here now for the fourth, if not the fifth time, and we expect him to come back again before the election because we took a view that Soweto is very important, very significant.

"You cannot win to decisively unless we have done exceedingly well in Soweto. And that is why we thought the president, as the campaigning chief of the African National Congress, will have to spend more time here to complement the work that is done by both our provincial and regional structures to get the population of this area to vote. And I think the president is being received very, very well," Ntuli said.

World.title: Who will get eThekwini?
World.content:
ETHEKWINI - eThekwini will be one of the most hotly-contested metros in the upcoming elections.

The Ground Work Collective's Mbali Ntuli said the metro's results will show how political support is shifting in KwaZulu-Natal and what this could mean for the ANC's future.

"I think that eThekwini is going to probably be the most interesting just because there are so many surprises in there. Just looking at the numbers of the party that's leading, I think that it's out of culture with the rest of the country but certainly is dominant in KZN and not just in the metro.

"I think it's going to be very exciting to unpack, personally, I think it's probably the one that people are looking at the most because it also signals a very important way for at least the ANC to think about a future.

World.title: Shock and grief in a Jordanian village after church attack
World.content:
AMMAN - Workers were cleaning the last traces of blood from St George's Church in Jordan's Hammoud the day after a deadly attack, when visitors arrived to express their solidarity amid an atmosphere of shock and grief.

At noon on Saturday, the bells of the Greek Orthodox church in Jordan's Karak Governorate, south of Amman, rang in unison alongside churches across Jordan, mourning the victims of the unprecedented attack against Christians in the kingdom, which left nine dead and 25 wounded according to the latest toll from the authorities.

Sayel al-Khaitan, a doctor who was inside the church when the attack, which took place during a funeral, began, described what happened as a tragedy.

"It is a criminal, dark, spiteful, Daesh-style attack", he said, referring to the Islamic State group, saying it targeted Jordanian society as a whole.

He described coming under heavy gunfire, saying, "It was likely that we would have fallen as martyrs in the massive attack, but, by a miracle, we survived".

Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya said the attackers were extremists.

They are still on the run.

On Sunday, eight of the nine victims were laid to rest next to the church, in a funeral that drew a huge crowd. Their flag-draped coffins were carried through the gathered masses, which included numerous religious figures and a large security presence, AFP images showed.

The ninth person, Mohammed al-Qasous, will be buried on Monday, his family said.

– 'Hunting people' –

Bullet holes marred the church's walls and wooden pews, with windows shattered and glass shards gathered into a pile outside.

Security forces have been deployed at the entrances and exits of the church in the small, predominantly Christian village.

Christians make up about three percent of the Muslim-majority kingdom.

On Saturday, preparations were underway for the victims' funerals the following day and church officials had dug a mass grave, which will become a memorial.

Father Yohanna Hamati told AFP about 170 to 200 people taking part in the funeral of a woman from his parish when the volley of bullets began outside shortly after 2 pm.

He said the mourners "at first did not grasp what was happening".

But as people fled into the church, "we began to realise there was an attack".

"They were hunting people," he said. "Nothing like it has ever happened, neither to a church nor to a mosque."

He said some of the wounded mourners were Muslim, adding "we make no distinction between Muslim and Christian" and stressing that what happened "does not reflect Jordanian morals".

In the village's guest hall, condolences were pouring in from clerics, military officials, the Vatican ambassador to Jordan and local dignitaries.

In the provincial capital Karak, dozens of people visited Prince Ali Military Hospital, where most of the wounded were taken, to donate blood or express solidarity.

Youth activist Murooj Al-Nuwaysa, wearing a pink hijab, said she came with about 25 young men and women, carrying a bouquet of flowers with a card reading, "Our loss is one".

– 'Shock and pain' –

Nuwaysa says she was at the hospital on Friday visiting a patient at the time of the attack.

"I didn't have my phone with me, and I didn't know what was happening."

"Ambulances were arriving in large numbers... It was very strange. Then there was the sight of the blood and the people... We later heard there had been an attack on a church," she said.

She said the youth delegation's visit on Saturday was an expression of "solidarity and our feeling of shock and pain."

"Our friends, colleagues and relatives, Muslims and Christians, live together and share each other's occasions. It is a huge shock."

Jordan's King Abdullah II visited the injured in the hospital, dressed in military fatigues and carrying a pistol on his hip.

"We will show them," he vowed to the victims.

Outside the hospital, Majed Jaafar, dressed in traditional Arab robes and the red-and-white Jordanian keffiyeh, said with a mix of sadness and anger: "We cried for them. Christians are cousins, neighbours and relatives. There is nothing between us but love."

"This is the first time something like this has happened in Jordan," he said.

Wisam al-Burqan, one of the villagers, said he arrived at the site of the attack minutes after the assailants fled.

"These people are not a danger to Christians alone... they are a danger to society as a whole," he said, demanding the government "strike with an iron fist, uproot them and show them no mercy".

By Mussa Hattar

World.title: Resignations alone won't fix systemic SAPS failures - expert
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Fannie Nkosi's resignation does not signify meaningful reform in the police service.

That's according to Unisa security analyst Jacob Mofokeng.

The organised crime unit member quit the service before an internal disciplinary hearing.

But he still faces criminal charges.

Mofokeng says radical structural changes are needed to fix the police.

"The fact that a member who was once regarded as a key witness before the Madlanga Commission now faces serious allegations of fraud, theft and defeating the ends of justice raises profound questions about integrity, accountability and organizational culture within the SAPS.

"At one level, the fact that allegations are being investigated and exposed may indicate that accountability mechanisms are beginning to function. However, the removal or resignation of individual members should not be mistaken for institutional reform. The real question is whether the substance address in the systematic conditions that enable corruption, misconduct and abuse of authority.

"True institutional reform will only begin when the National Commissioner General Fannie Masemola implements radical structural changes to dismantle systematic governance failures. We have been waiting then for the implementation of the advisory board. We welcome that kind of structures within the criminal justice system. It's yet to be realized whether indeed there is the political will for such structure to operate within that particular domain."

World.title: eNCA MarkData Election Survey | Here's what the results mean
World.content:
Former President Jacob Zuma’s MK Party has an excellent shot at winning an overall majority in the eThekwini metro in Durban, according to the eNCA MarkData poll has found.

For the relevant full eThekwini poll results, please click here.

In the Tshwane metro, according to the poll, the DA will be the largest party by a wide margin, but it will almost certainly not obtain an overall majority.

For the relevant full Tshwane poll results, please click here.

The results of the polls for Tshwane (which encompasses Pretoria and surrounding areas) and eThekwini were announced in a live broadcast on eNCA this morning.

The poll presumes a turnout of 48,8% for the election on 4 November, and the margin of error for each metro is about 3%.

For a full description of the poll’s methodology, please click here.

The relevant full results of the eNCA MarkData poll for Nelson Mandela Bay can be found here, for Ekurhuleni here, for Johannesburg here, and for Cape Town here.

In eThekwini, MK is polling at 48%, followed by the DA on 25,2%. The ANC figures mirror its 2024 electoral meltdown, with the IFP the only other party above the 5% support level in KwaZulu Natal’s only metro.

The nation’s capital, based in the Tshwane metro, produced a completely different polling result, with the DA on 33,9% and the ANC on 24,3%. Supporters of the EFF, Action SA and the Freedom Front Plus will take heart from their relatively strong polling results in Tshwane.

Tshwane mayor Nasiphi Moya has clearly impressed voters – she is more than twice as popular as Action SA, the party which she represents. All other Tshwane mayoral candidates poll lower than their respective political parties.

In both eThekwini and Tshwane, respondents blame the ANC for service delivery issues, with water being a major issue in both metros, and the poor response to flood damage crippling the ANC in eThekwini.

In both metros, ANC candidates are also handicapped by their party’s inability to decide on mayoral candidates.

World.title: I will go for Senate, Governor Muthomi Njuki declares
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Njuki declared his interest in the Senate seat, even as a proposed law seeking to bar governors from running for the position before 10 years have passed is pending. [File, Standard]

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki will vie for a Senate seat in next year’s General Election.

Njuki, who doubles up as the chairperson of the Council of Governors, declared his interest in the Senate seat, even as a proposed law seeking to bar governors from running for the position before 10 years have passed is pending.

His announcement brings the number of aspirants to at least four, so far.

Former governor Mbae Ragwa from Maara and who served for one term (2013-2017), has announced his bid for the senator's seat too.

Senator Mwenda Gataya, who won the seat on President William Ruto's United Democratic Alliance (UDA) in 2022, has opted not to seek re-election, and will instead vie for MP of Tharaka constituency, currently held by Gitonga Murugara, also of UDA.

Mr Murugara plans to vie for Governor, as does Woman Representative Susan Ngugi.

Former Chuka University Vice Chancellor Prof Erastus Njoka, from Chuka-Igambang'ombe constituency, and who Njuki beat in 2022, will make a second stab at the seat.

Governor Njuki, who served as Chuka-Igambang'ombe MP before he won the seat, said he was firmly in the race for Senate.

"Muthomi Njuki will next vie for Senator of Tharaka-Nithi County. Those who were doing their political arithmetic without including me in the race should do their calculations again,” he said.

Njuki said he wanted to be in the Senate to be able to protect the interests of Tharaka Nithi people, and the resources the devolved unit gets from the central government.

"I want to be a senator with a difference, and I will protect the development resources that come to Tharaka Nithi," he said in Maara.

Not long ago, Njuki stoked political controversy when he said Chuka-Igambang'ombe constituency, where he comes from, should not produce the next governor.

He was of the view that the seat should go to either Maara or Tharaka constituency.

"It is being mean for the people of Chuka/Igambang’ombe constituency where I come from to claim governorship in 2027 after having it for 10 years. It is time for either Tharaka or Maara,” Njuki said at the time, but he has since retracted his remarks.

He said: "The people have asked me not to say who I want as governor. I have said I will leave them to decide and I will hand over the instruments of power and records to whoever they elect."

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: The Iran war’s toxic impact on one of the planet’s most unique seas
World.content:
Abu Dhabi —

The conflict in the Middle East is shaping up to be yet another US war with a toxic legacy.

Bombs and missiles have released heavy metals and harmful chemicals into the atmosphere. US-Israeli and Iranian strikes have hit oil facilities, igniting fires that covered Tehran in thick black smoke and oil-saturated rain, exposing millions to pollution which could have long-lasting health impacts.

And these strikes are also affecting the Persian Gulf. Attacks on ships and oil infrastructure in the waterway have produced oil spills visible from space.

A spill from a tanker has temporarily closed beaches in the Emirate of Umm Al Quwain with authorities working to contain the environmental impacts, according to an announcement Thursday by the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment.

It’s not been confirmed whether the spill is linked to Iranian attacks but it’s yet another sign of the huge risks faced by the Persian Gulf, one of the world’s most delicate and unique marine systems.

As the conflict continues, experts are warning of a broader contamination crisis.

A surge in oil pollution

For months, cargo ships and oil tankers have been targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, the vital shipping route for oil and gas between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

The progression from vessel impact to environmental damage is clear to see in many cases, said Brian Barnes, who is part of a group of satellite oceanographers at the University of South Florida analyzing the effects of this war from afar.

“Some of the major ships that have been targeted, we see prolonged plumes, stretching for hundreds of kilometers away from the impact site,” Barnes said.

The Persian Gulf has long suffered from oil pollution, but research by Barnes and other scientists comparing March 2026, when fighting was intense, with the same period last year shows a sharp increase.

An oil tanker burns after being hit by an Iranian strike in the ship-to-ship transfer zone at Khor al-Zubair port near Basra, Iraq, March 11, 2026. AP

“What we’re seeing is twice the amount of surface oil in the Persian Gulf area relative to what we would expect in the absence of a major conflict,” Barnes said.

Although, he noted, satellite imagery can only show what is on the surface of the water and not the thickness of the oil, which would give a more accurate picture of the extent of the contamination.

What is harder to assess with limited physical access to the conflict-riddled waterway is the impact on marine wildlife.

One of the planet’s most unique ecosystems

The Persian Gulf hosts an ecosystem teeming with life. It is home to several species of sea turtles, hundreds of species of fish and the world’s second-largest population of dugongs, or sea cows.

“One of the world’s largest whale shark congregations occurs close to the South Pars oil field where Qatar and Iran meet,” said Bernhard Riegl, a professor at Nova Southeastern University who has studied the Persian Gulf for decades.

Sandy offshore islands and expansive seagrass beds make the Gulf an ideal habitat for nesting and breeding. Extensive mangrove forests and coral reef structures create protected nurseries for dolphins, seabirds, and whale sharks. Yet in springtime, traditionally the season for breeding, the war was raging.

A view of the vibrant underwater world at one of Musandam’s popular diving sites in Khasab, Oman on August 28, 2025. Mahmut Serdar Alakus/Anadolu/Getty Images

A satellite image shows oil in the Persian Gulf on April 2, 2026. Sentinel-2/European Space Agency

Only the hardiest marine life survives in these waters. Not only is the Persian Gulf one of the world’s hottest seas, but it also experiences sharp temperature changes throughout the year.

The water near Kuwait City, for example, goes from highs of around 36 degrees Celsius (97 Fahrenheit) in the height of summer to lows of around 16 degrees Celsius (60 Fahrenheit).

Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, the UAE’s special envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs for Nature, called for an end to attacks on the Gulf in an editorial earlier this year.

“While the financial costs of damage can be calculated, the loss of ecosystems and species cannot. Once degraded, these systems may not recover,” she wrote.

⛅ Get CNN Weather in your inbox The forecast is just the beginning. We’ll send you expert coverage and the stories behind the weather — so you always know more than just the number. 

A looming catastrophe

Contamination in the Gulf brings unique challenges as the body of water is relatively shallow — the deepest areas are only around 360 feet — and it is small, at 93,000 square miles. It also has only one entry and exit point connecting it to the open ocean: the Strait of Hormuz, which leads into the Gulf of Oman and the Indian Ocean beyond. This all means pollutants tend not to disperse or dilute easily.

No matter which country or vessel may be a target during this war, the repercussions will have wide impacts, Riegl said: “If we take a drop of oil and put it into the water on the Iranian side of the inflow into the Gulf, a year later it will be in Kuwait, two years later it will be on the Omani side of the Gulf and float out there.”

The 1991 Gulf War should be a cautionary tale, Riegl said. Retreating Iraqi forces set fire to hundreds of oil wells in Kuwait creating an environmental catastrophe felt throughout the Gulf.

An oil well fire at the Greater Burhan oil field in Kuwait, in August 9, 1991. Per-Anders Pettersson/Hulton Archive/Getty Images

“The shorelines were devastatingly affected,” Riegl said. “In fact, in many areas of Saudi (Arabia), if you go and dig in the sand, there’s still old oil in there. It’s just very hard to get rid of.”

An additional concern is the fact that tens of millions of Gulf residents rely on desalination plants, which convert seawater into drinking water.

The six countries which form the Gulf Cooperation Council produce around a third of the world’s desalinated water. Bahrain and Kuwait are almost entirely dependent on desalination for all drinking water. Oil pollution in the Gulf could damage these facilities, imperiling water supply.

When hundreds of millions of gallons were intentionally released into the Persian Gulf during the Iraq war, Kuwait had to rely on Saudi Arabia, Turkey and others to provide hundreds of water tankers and trucks to deliver bottled water.

A natural laboratory

One perhaps unexpected repercussion of environmental damage in the Persian Gulf is that it could undermine scientists’ understanding of the impacts climate change will have on the world’s seas.

The Gulf’s high temperatures are roughly where marine tropics are expected to be around the year 2100, Riegl said.

A flock of birds near the shores of the Daymaniyat Islands Nature Reserve in Oman, on October 4, 2023. Karim Sahib/AFP/Getty Images

The Gulf has “some of the most… valuable genetics of any sea on Earth, because a lot of the adaptation that will need to be done has already been achieved in the Gulf.”

“If we want to know what the ocean at large will look like at the end of the century,”he added, “the Gulf is the area to look at.”

World.title: Foreign citizen beaten to death during march in South Africa as anti-immigrant tensions flare
World.content:
Cape Town, South Africa AP — A foreign citizen was beaten to death by a group of around 50 people during a protest march in South Africa’s east coast city of Durban, police said Thursday, as A foreign citizen was beaten to death by a group of around 50 people during a protest march in South Africa’s east coast city of Durban, police said Thursday, as anti-immigrant tensions continue to flare in Africa’s most advanced economy

Police said the group approached the man, who was standing at the side of a road during a march through the streets of Durban’s city center, and assaulted him.

Police did not immediately give the man’s nationality or details on what the march was related to. They said the victim was in his 30s or early 40s, and they were still trying to identify suspects in the attack.

South Africa has struggled with months of anti-immigration tensions. Marches calling for government action against migrants in the country illegally have sometimes spilled over into violence.

Nigeria, Mozambique, Malawi and other countries have said some of their citizens have been killed in xenophobic attacks linked to the anti-immigration protests. South African authorities have disputed some of those claims and said some deaths were related to criminal activity and not the protests.

Tens of thousands of migrants have left South Africa in recent months in one of the biggest mass exoduses in years. Many cite the threat of violence from angry locals, though the government also said that many were deported for not having the proper documents to be in South Africa.

As Africa’s biggest economy, South Africa attracts migrants from many nations on the continent, but that has sometimes brought tensions within communities because of the country’s extremely high unemployment rate and overburdened public services.

Durban, South Africa’s third-biggest city of nearly four million people, has become a hotspot for the anti-immigrant tensions that have surged this year.

In June, thousands of migrants mainly from Malawi gathered at a park in the city seeking to be repatriated to their home country. They claimed they were fleeing threats of violence after a protest group demanded undocumented migrants leave South Africa by June 30.

The camp of migrants seeking to leave grew so quickly that authorities had to build more temporary accommodation centers to handle the numbers.

This month, cars were torched and shops were looted in the Johannesburg township of Soweto after a court ruling made it easier for foreign citizens to claim asylum in South Africa, leading to many making applications at government buildings and sparking a reaction from locals.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has denounced violence related to immigration but has also acknowledged failures in the border control system over the years that have allowed migrants to travel to and stay in South Africa without documentation.

South Africa’s official government figures show there are around 2.4 million foreign nationals among the country’s population of 62 million, but protesters say there are many more in South Africa without documentation who haven’t been counted.

World.title: Macron says Paris suburb shooting that killed one person was terrorist and racist act
World.content:
Paris Reuters — A gunman killed one person and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in a shooting in a Paris suburb that French President Emmanuel Macron described as a “terrorist and racist” attack.

“What happened today is, I am telling you, a turning point, because it is the first time we have had a terrorist act that was planned to kill our compatriots, our children, based on the colour of their skin or their religion,” Macron told reporters.

The shooting happened earlier on Friday when the gunman fired an automatic weapon at a petrol station, a medical center and a children’s playground in Trappes, on the Paris outskirts.

Officials said a 39-year-old suspect, whom they named as Kevin T, had been arrested. His family surname was not given, as is common practice in such criminal inquiries in France.

The shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests turned violent last Saturday and before further demonstrations this coming weekend.

Some far-right politicians have blamed immigration for looting and vandalism in a number of French cities on October 17.

Macron said the gunman had deliberately chosen not to fire upon some people due to their skin colour and appearance.

The anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office, known as PNAT, formally opened an investigation into the shooting.

PNAT can take over any criminal investigation it believes meets the criteria for terrorism, including violence inspired by far-right ideas. Terrorism sentences are tougher, and counter-terrorism forces have greater investigative powers.

Broadcaster BFM said the wounded girl had been hit eight times and was in serious condition.

Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh, whose parents came from Morocco, said the shooting was “racist” and “Islamophobic.”

“The people targeted today could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law,” said Rabeh.

Rabeh called for a collective condemnation of rhetoric that “ideologically arms those capable of carrying out such acts.”

Nicolas Dainville, the mayor of nearby La Verriere, said the suspect was “of a European type.” Rabeh said two of the victims were of African and North African origin, respectively, and did not provide details about the backgrounds of the other victims.

Video images showed the suspect’s car riddled with bullets.

This story is breaking and will be updated.

World.title: Egyptian economist rules out US dollar falling below LE 50
World.content:
Economist Mohamed Fouad suggests that the US dollar exchange rate in Egypt will likely hover around the LE 52 mark for the time being.

He sees it unlikely that the rate will drop below LE 50 in the near term, citing pressures from the outflow of foreign investments, rising financing requirements, and structural imbalances within the Egyptian economy.

During a phone-in with “al-Hekaya” (The Story), hosted by Amr Adib on MBC Masr, Fouad explained that the dollar’s rise is occurring against the backdrop of a global trend of US currency strength.

He noted that this coincides with three primary factors: economic conditions in the US, pressures within energy markets, and structural issues in the Egyptian economy.

Fouad pointed out that the immediate cause for the dollar’s rise in Egypt is that capital outflows are exceeding inflows; he cited the exit of approximately US$1.8 billion in just four days—from Monday to Thursday of the previous week.

He added that a flexible exchange rate regime makes the market more sensitive to the movement of capital inflows and outflows.

Why is the dollar rising globally?

Fouad said that the US economy is experiencing robust activity, bolstered by a strong labor market and high consumer spending.

This coincides with energy-related risks and massive financing requirements that are absorbing liquidity from the markets.

He explained that the US budget deficit, and the approximately $2.2 trillion in new debt issuance expected from the US Treasury represent a significant source of demand for financing.

Fouad also pointed to projections that new offerings in the technology sector could reach around $1.7 trillion by 2027, further enhancing the appeal of the US market for liquidity inflows.

He added that these pressures are not limited to Egypt but extend to other emerging markets, noting that Argentina is facing acute financing strains, with its bond yields approaching 12 percent – meanwhile, Indonesia faces the threat of being removed from emerging market indices, and Turkey has received a warning in this regard.

Outflow of Foreign Investments

Regarding domestic factors, Fouad explained that the outflow of dollars from the Egyptian market is primarily linked to two types of foreign investment activity: first, the exit of investors selling off their holdings of treasury bills; and second, the maturity of three-month deals concluded in July, which allows investors to recover their funds and transfer them abroad.

He noted that a flexible exchange rate regime allows the impact of these movements to be reflected directly in the dollar exchange rate—particularly when capital outflows exceed inflows.

Fouad further pointed out that global pressures are coinciding with structural imbalances within the Egyptian economy, as evidenced by balance-of-payments indicators; the trade deficit stands at approximately $65 billion, while the current account deficit is nearly $2.25 billion.

He concluded that the convergence of global financing pressures and domestic imbalances leaves the Egyptian economy increasingly vulnerable to fluctuations in international markets and capital flows.

Dollar Outlook

Fouad ruled out a catastrophe in the conventional sense, but emphasized that the Egyptian economy is facing clear and persistent pressures—part of a broader trend affecting various emerging markets.

Given these circumstances, Fouad suggested that the dollar exchange rate is likely to hover around the 52-pound mark for the time being, noting that a return to levels below LE 50 in the near term is unlikely.

Post-IMF Plan

Regarding the national plan for the period following the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program, Fouad explained that discussions are still in the phase of defining broad outlines.

It has been agreed to open the plan for public debate until the end of next December; he emphasized that it has not yet reached the stage of a fully detailed plan.

He also noted his participation in a session on public debt and foreign currency resource management, held as part of the Egypt 2026 Forum.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: The iPhone Duo is Apple’s coolest phone in years. There’s just one problem
World.content:
There were many times I didn’t want to put the iPhone Duo down. Once you get used to reading, watching TV and scrolling through Instagram on a giant screen, it’s hard to go back to a tiny glowing rectangle.

There’s just one issue: Many apps are still made for that little rectangle.

This is what it’s been like to use the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone, which launches on October 23. It starts at $2,000, making it as expensive as Apple’s latest 14-inch MacBook Pro.

It’s a big move for Apple, which rarely messes with the winning formula that’s turned the iPhone into a business that raked in more than $200 billion in revenue last year. But after years of incremental iPhone updates, Apple faced pressure to prove it could still captivate consumers.

I got a taste of that future after spending about a week with the new foldable phone that Apple provided CNN for testing purposes. The iPhone Duo became my tablet for watching Netflix, a bedside alarm clock at night, an extra screen for watching football on Sunday, a miniature monitor when connected to my Bluetooth keyboard and a camera with a built-in tripod.

But there were equally as many times – if not more – when I grew frustrated because apps didn’t work the way they should, since developers haven’t updated them yet. And despite Apple’s “it just works” approach, the iPhone Duo takes some getting used to. While the iPhone Duo’s software certainly felt much smoother and more fluid than Android alternatives, many of its core features have been available on Samsung or Google phones for years.

The iPhone Duo’s inner screen is almost the size of an iPad Mini. Zoe Todd/CNN You can prop the iPhone Duo open to use it as a bedside clock. Zoe Todd/CNN

What can iPhone Duo do that a regular phone can’t?

The iPhone Duo is the biggest change Apple has made to the iPhone in its nearly 20-year history. There’s a 5.4-inch screen on the outside, which unfolds to reveal a 7.6-inch display on the inside. When closed, the iPhone Duo feels like a passport, but obviously thicker and heavier. When opened, it’s like a thinner and smaller iPad Mini.

One of the most popular questions I get about the iPhone Duo is whether you see the crease. The answer, believe it or not, is no. The crease is barely visible when using apps or scrolling around the home screen, and I can hardly feel it when swiping across the display.

The iPhone Duo’s unconventional shape means it can do things you wouldn’t be able to do as easily with a regular phone. Prop it open like a tent or stand it up like a book while the screen is locked, and the display will turn into a bedside clock, digital photo frame or calendar. Certain apps like the camera and Apple Fitness Plus will shift to the top portion of the screen when folded halfway like a laptop – but that depends on whether developers program their apps to do it.

The iPhone Duo works when folded halfway, but not all apps are optimized for it yet. Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

The iPhone Duo (right) alongside a passport (middle) and Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 (left). Zoe Todd/CNN The iPhone Duo can run two apps at the same time. Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

When the phone is open, you can take selfies with the phone’s rear cameras while viewing a preview on the cover screen, which came in handy when I was shooting the video for this review.

The iPhone Duo can run two apps on screen at the same time, which was useful for situations that involved looking up information or viewing content in multiple apps. You can, for example, drag and drop an image straight from the Photos app into a text message when both apps are on screen. I also used split screen mode to show a friend my Halloween costume and the movie character it’s based on at the same time.

While this is convenient, it’s probably not the reason you’re going to buy an iPhone Duo. The Duo’s inner screen is best used when dedicating the whole thing to a single app like Netflix. And the display has a matte finish, which reduces glare and doesn’t smudge easily.

But many apps, including popular ones like Google Maps, Gmail, Call of Duty Mobile, and Uber weren’t updated to take full advantage of this big screen when I tested the Duo before launch. Some apps looked like floating windows in the middle of the tablet-sized screen.

These apps can expand to occupy more of the display, but they still don’t fill the whole space. Other apps were updated to occupy most of the display but still had a black bar along the side. That’s what you see when developers haven’t updated their apps using Apple’s latest software development tools, as the company lays out on its website.

Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

The good news is that more apps have been updated even during the few days I’ve had the phone, including Google, TikTok, Instagram and Threads. But the uncertainty of not knowing how an app is going to look feels inconsistent and can be jarring – which is an area where Android has had a head start.

The apps that are optimized for the Duo provide a glimpse of what’s possible. My favorite app so far is the puzzle platform game Planet of Lana, which looks gorgeous and colorful on the Duo’s larger screen.

I also really liked using Apple Books, which lets you view pages on either side of the screen when the display is slightly folded like a real book. (Amazon’s Kindle app is one of the many apps that hasn’t been updated yet). Apple’s Messages and Mail apps also show your inbox on the left and messages on the right so that you can see everything at once.

But how is it as a regular phone?

For its price, the iPhone Duo should be able to do everything a regular phone can do and more. My biggest concern was that the design would make it feel awkward to use when closed, but typing and swiping on the cover screen feels surprisingly natural and comfortable. I’ve even come to prefer the Duo’s wider keyboard over the one on my iPhone 18 Pro.

The iPhone 18 Pro (left) alongside the iPhone Duo (right) Zoe Todd/CNN

Still, there was a learning curve at first. I kept accidentally hitting the Siri button, which is located on the Duo’s side, when I meant to press the volume keys on the top of the phone. I also didn’t realize that you must have an app open before you can use split screen mode, rather than just opening a new app and dragging it to one side of the display from the home screen.

Battery life is reasonable and in line with what you’d expect from a new phone. My battery was usually down to 35% or 46% by the time I went to bed, although that will always vary depending on which apps you’re using and how often you’re using the tablet screen compared to the cover display.

iPhone 18 Pro zoom (comparison to iPhone Duo zoom) Lisa Eadicicco/CNN iPhone Duo zoom (comparison to iPhone 18 Pro zoom) Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

The iPhone Duo has cameras that are similar to the iPhone 18 Pro’s but with one key difference: there’s no telephoto camera. That means zoomed-in photos won’t look as crisp or clear compared to ones taken on the iPhone 18 Pro, although shots captured on both phones looked similar otherwise.

The biggest question I get about the iPhone Duo is whether it’s worth the $2,000. That’s tough to answer considering it costs more than a month’s rent for most Americans . The only reason you should even consider it is if you really want a screen that’s bigger than you’d find on any other phone but still fits in your pocket.

My advice? Wait until developers have had more time to optimize their apps before you decide. While the Duo is compelling, apps still have catching up to do.

World.title: Agreement ends St. Catherine’s Monastery dispute between Egypt and Greece
World.content:
Egypt has welcomed the consent of the Archbishop of the St. Catherine’s Monastery to sign an agreement regulating the legal status of the monastery and its surrounding lands in the Sinai Peninsula.

In a statement issued on Saturday, the Egyptian Foreign Ministry announced that Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty received a letter from Archbishop Symeon, confirming his agreement to sign the contract, RT reported on Saturday.

The formal signing ceremony will take place at a date to be determined through coordination between the two sides.

This development follows a years-long legal dispute concerning the status of the monastery and its surrounding territory.

The situation intensified in May 2025, when a ruling by the Ismailia Court of Appeals raised concerns regarding the monastery’s rights over certain lands and facilities essential to its monastic life.

Lawsuit dating over a decade

The case stems from a lawsuit filed by Egyptian government authorities in 2015 concerning dozens of plots of land—a dispute centered on state ownership versus the monastery’s rights to possess and utilize the property.

The ruling affirmed state ownership of the disputed land, while distinguishing between religious and archaeological sites and other types of land.

This raised concerns within Greek ecclesiastical circles regarding the future of the monastery and the rights of its monks.

The dispute has also impacted Egyptian-Greek relations, prompting Athens to seek a settlement that ensures the preservation of the monastery’s Greek Orthodox character and its continued religious role.

Cairo has emphasized that the ruling does not diminish the monastery’s spiritual and historical standing, and that the monks will be able to continue performing religious rites at the site.

Agreement drafted

As communications between the two sides continued, an agreement was drafted to clarify the legal status of the monastery and its associated lands, and to establish a framework for implementing the judicial ruling—ensuring the continuity of monastic life while upholding the rights of the Egyptian state.

Efforts to reach this agreement were supported by the Church of Greece, as well as various other Orthodox leaders and churches.

The Foreign Egyptian Ministry’s statement expressed the state’s high regard for the over 1,600 year-old monastery, and reaffirmed its commitment to preserving its religious standing and heritage, recognizing it as a symbol of tolerance and coexistence among religions and civilizations.

The signing of this agreement is set to pave the way for concluding the legal proceedings related to the dispute and mitigating any potential impact on Egyptian-Greek relations, all while safeguarding the monastery’s religious and historical status, in full compliance with Egyptian legislation and the state’s sovereignty over its territory.

World.title: Egypt’s government says it has no intention to increase fuel prices
World.content:
Egypt’s government has denied any intention to implement electricity load-shedding or to pass the burden of rising oil prices onto citizens, clarifying that no such decisions have been made.

In a phone interview with the “Modern MTI” television channel on Friday evening, Cabinet spokesperson Mohamed Adel emphasized the importance of verifying the accuracy of information circulating regarding the energy sector.

Energy prices are a significant issue for both citizens and investors, Adel said, given their direct impact on economic activities and production costs.

He emphasized the importance of referring to full statements and official sources, rather than relying on fragmented clips that could lead to a misunderstanding of the government’s positions—particularly regarding the energy sector.

Adel noted that Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has stressed the need to confront rumors and counter misinformation—a point also underscored by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly—as part of the state’s commitment to clarifying the facts for its citizens.

The government is managing the issue of energy conservation in light of current developments and challenges, Adel assured, while highlighting the importance of verifying information before sharing it—especially given that this issue directly impacts citizens, as well as activities within the investment and industrial sectors.

World.title: PM responds to claims that citizens do not feel development fruits
World.content:
CAIRO, Oct 24 (MENA) – Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stated during the closing ceremony of the Egypt 2026 Forum today, under the auspices of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, that some attempt to project a mental image that the citizen does not feel the fruits of development, affirming that what the historical presentation included today is sufficient to answer this question.

Madbouly added before concluding his speech that to the great people of Egypt, what this historical presentation included is sufficient to answer this question, and for those who want details, the total beneficiaries targeted by the presidential initiative Hayah Karima is 61 million citizens, with the first phase ending now benefiting 18 million citizens including 11 million citizens in Upper Egypt, asking whether these did not feel the fruits of development.

He added that the state managed to eliminate unsafe areas by executing housing units for about 1.5 million citizens, asking whether they did not feel the fruits of development, noting that without state intervention with these citizens, their fate would have been like others who died under rocks, lost their lives in torrent paths, or were electrocuted under high voltage wires.

He continued that the fruits of development enabled the state to spend billions of pounds on our people without any return for the government except the greatest, most important, and best return, which is protecting them from death, protecting their children, and working to secure a better future for them, and the reward for this with God is great.

He noted that 5.5 million citizens are currently registered in the first phase of the comprehensive health insurance system in the governorates of Port Said, Luxor, Ismailia, South Sinai, Suez, and Aswan, asking whether these do not enjoy the fruits of development, and 63 million citizens were screened and those in need treated for Hepatitis C, asking whether these did not return to life once again after their future was threatened.

Madbouli stated that 3.3 million operations were conducted to eliminate waiting lists, asking whether these millions did not benefit from the fruits of development, and two million families benefited from Sakan Kol Al-Masryeen projects and developing governorate capitals, asking whether this unprecedented number did not benefit from the fruits of development, besides eight million residents inhabiting unplannned areas developed by the state.

He added that the Suez Canal Economic Zone attracted investments providing 164,000 job opportunities, asking whether these youth and hundreds of thousands of others did not benefit from the fruits of development, besides 50,000 job opportunities provided by industrial complexes.

He continued that 16.2 million families benefited from efforts to connect natural gas to homes, and 8.3 million families benefited from support efforts for families most in need, among them 4.7 million families currently benefiting from the cash support program, 2.2 million families exited after their social and economic conditions improved, and 1.4 million families exited as a result of changing circumstances.

He completed that current average classroom density reached about 45 students compared to 100 students per classroom before 2014, asking whether they benefited or not, and the 150,000 teachers initiative to solve the teacher shortage problem benefited teachers, their families, students, and even the entire society.

Madbouli stated that until 2014, 10 or 12 percent of Egypt’s villages had sewage, and currently the percentage has become approximately 60 percent, asking whether all these citizens did not feel the fruits of development, affirming they certainly felt it, and hundreds of thousands of citizens used to ride trains without doors or windows along with breakdowns, while currently we have air-conditioned trains passing through Egypt’s villages, and we have a high-speed electric train, a light rail transit, a monorail, and endless phases of the subway. (MENA)

World.title: Liberia: Judge Cites Evidence in Finding NSA Staff Peter Bon Jallah Guilty of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Criminal Court E Acquits Him of Gang Rape; Orders Pre-Sentence Report Before Sentencing

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonsus Wesseh Sr. has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping, but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.



In a verdict delivered Friday, October 23, Judge Wesseh said he had reviewed the evidence presented by both parties and considered the arguments advanced during the trial before determining that the prosecution had established sufficient grounds to convict Jallah on two of the three charges.

The judge framed his decision around three central questions: whether the prosecution’s evidence justified a conviction for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

He answered the first question in the negative, acquitting Jallah of gang rape, but answered the other two in the affirmative, finding him guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah remanded at Monrovia Central Prison pending the submission of a pre-sentence and behavioral report by the Bureau of Probation Services at the Ministry of Justice.

The judge directed the clerk of court to communicate with the probation authorities to ensure that the report is made available as soon as possible to assist the court in determining the appropriate sentence.

Judge Identifies Three Decisive Questions

In his ruling, Judge Wesseh said the court had examined the facts and circumstances contained in the evidence presented at trial before identifying three issues that were decisive to the case.

On the gang rape charge, the judge concluded that the prosecution’s evidence did not provide sufficient and reasonable grounds to convict Jallah. He consequently declared the defendant not guilty and acquitted him of that charge.

However, on statutory rape, the judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution provided sufficient grounds for conviction.

He reached a similar conclusion on the kidnapping charge, finding Jallah guilty on that count as well.

The ruling represents a split decision in a case that involved allegations of repeated sexual abuse of a minor and the alleged confinement of the complainant for several days.

Indictment Details Alleged Repeated Abuse

According to the indictment summarized in the court’s verdict, Jallah and two unidentified men were indicted by the Montserrado County Grand Jury during the February 2026 Term of Court for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

The indictment alleged that Jallah and the two other men acted individually and jointly in sexually abusing the complainant on multiple occasions.

It further stated that the complainant, who was 16 at the time of the alleged incidents, lived in the Airfield Shark Community in Monrovia and regularly visited Jallah’s residence to perform domestic work for which he received compensation.

The indictment alleged that on November 29 and December 24, 2025, Jallah lured the boy to his residence in the Sharks Community of Airfield Sinkor, where he allegedly sexually assaulted him.

The most serious allegations concerned an incident said to have occurred on January 1, 2026, after the boy participated in a community football league at the Kpelle Town football field.

According to the indictment, the boy encountered Jallah near his residence after the game. Jallah allegedly offered to purchase football boots for him and instructed him to return home to bathe before accompanying him.

The indictment alleged that the two subsequently travelled by car to a building in the Camp Johnson Road area of downtown Monrovia, where the boy was allegedly held for three days and sexually abused by Jallah and the two unidentified men.

It further alleged that on January 3, 2026, at about 10 p.m., the boy was concealed at the back of Jallah’s vehicle and abandoned along 15th Street in Sinkor.

The complainant was reportedly rescued by private security guards, who alerted his parents. His mother and other relatives subsequently took him to the John F. Kennedy Medical Center for medical examinations.

These details formed part of the allegations contained in the indictment and should not be interpreted as separate findings by the court unless expressly established in the judge’s ruling.

Case Faced Procedural Delays

The court’s verdict also outlined the procedural history of the case, which experienced several delays before proceeding to a full trial.

The case was initially before Criminal Assizes Court “A” for Montserrado County before being transferred to Criminal Court “E” for evidentiary proceedings and a full trial.

Jallah was arraigned on June 18, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the indictment. He subsequently elected to be tried by a judge without a jury.

The trial was delayed after the prosecution filed a motion seeking a change of venue. Following the denial of that motion, the prosecution petitioned the Chamber Justice for a writ of certiorari, but the petition was denied and the case was ordered to proceed.

The proceedings encountered another setback when the judge previously presiding over the matter could not continue taking evidence after the regular sitting of the court expired.

On August 5, 2026, the case was reassigned for trial.

According to the written verdict, the prosecution presented 13 regular witnesses and six rebuttal witnesses, while the defense called eight regular witnesses and three subpoenaed witnesses from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Orange GSM and the John F. Kennedy Medical Center.

The prosecution’s witnesses included the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The defense witnesses included Jallah himself and several other individuals who testified on his behalf.

The number of witnesses listed in the written verdict differs from earlier accounts that referred to 12 prosecution witnesses, making the court’s official record the appropriate reference for the final tally.

DNA and Medical Evidence Featured at Trial

The prosecution relied in part on forensic findings linking Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, testimony attributed to the forensic examiner indicated that the findings could not establish precisely when or how the biological material was deposited.

The defense challenged the prosecution’s interpretation of the evidence, pointing to alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Medical evidence also featured prominently in the proceedings. Earlier accounts of the trial referenced a John F. Kennedy Medical Center report that reportedly found no visible signs of anal trauma, while the parties disputed the significance of the medical and forensic findings.

The precise weight the court assigned to each item of evidence should be established from the complete written ruling and trial record. The verdict provided identifies the court’s conclusions on the three charges but does not detail its assessment of every witness or exhibit.

Prosecution and Defense Clash in Final Arguments

During final arguments on Thursday, October 22, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged Judge Wesseh to convict Jallah, maintaining that the evidence presented during the trial supported the charges.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh argued that the prosecution had failed to prove its case to the required legal standard. The defense questioned the police investigation and challenged the interpretation of the medical, forensic and testimonial evidence.

The judge adjourned the proceedings until Friday morning to review the evidence and arguments before delivering the verdict.

In reaching his decision, Judge Wesseh found the prosecution’s evidence sufficient to convict Jallah of statutory rape and kidnapping, while concluding that it did not warrant a conviction for gang rape.

The two other men named in the indictment were not brought under the court’s jurisdiction and were not tried alongside Jallah in these proceedings.

Defense Plans Appeal

Following the verdict, defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia.

The planned appeal would give the defense an opportunity to challenge the lower court’s decision before the country’s highest court.

In the meantime, Jallah remains ordered remanded at Monrovia Central Prison while the Bureau of Probation Services prepares the report requested by Judge Wesseh.

The report is intended to assist the court in determining the sentence to be imposed following the guilty verdicts.

The case now enters the sentencing stage before the anticipated appeal, with the court having found Jallah guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but acquitted him of gang rape.

World.title: Liberia: Court Finds Peter Bon Jallah Guilty Of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

— Acquits NSA Staff of Gang Rape; Defense Announces Supreme Court Appeal

MONROVIA, Liberia — Criminal Court “E” at the Temple of Justice has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.

By Victoria Wesseh



The verdict was handed down Friday, October 23, 2026, by Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonso Wesseh Sr., following final arguments by the prosecution and defense on Thursday.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah’s remand at Monrovia Central Prison. However, the court had not announced the sentence at the time of reporting.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh has announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia, setting the stage for another legal battle over the verdict.

The court acquitted Jallah of gang rape. The two other individuals allegedly involved in the incident on Camp Johnson Road were not presented during the trial.

Prosecution Presented 12 Witnesses

During the trial, prosecutors presented 12 witnesses, including the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel, and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The prosecution also relied on DNA findings that linked Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, the forensic examiner reportedly testified that the findings could not establish when or how the biological material was deposited.

Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Defense Challenges Evidence, Plans Appeal

During Thursday’s final arguments, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged the court to convict Jallah, arguing that the evidence presented during the trial supported a guilty verdict.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh countered that the prosecution had failed to establish the allegations beyond a reasonable doubt. The defense questioned the interpretation of medical and forensic findings, as well as aspects of the police investigation.

The competing arguments centered on witness testimony, medical findings, forensic evidence, and whether the prosecution had sufficiently established the elements of the charged offenses.

With the guilty verdict on two charges and the defense’s announced intention to appeal, the case is expected to proceed to the Supreme Court, where Jallah’s lawyers will seek a review of the lower court’s decision.

This news is breaking. More details to follow.
