World.title: Iraq increases port capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past.

The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers.

Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion.

Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr.

SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

World.title: Iraq advances Japanese loan port projects as Grand Faw reach 98%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework.

The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority.

The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities.

The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion.

Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%.

Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani.

Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

World.title: Iraq to construct six dams with Turkey and 13 rainwater harvesting barriers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors.

The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package.

In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites.

An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

World.title: Rain showers and cloud cover forecast across provinces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Meteorological Organization and Seismology forecast fluctuating cloud cover across the country over the coming days, with localized rainfall expected to begin on Tuesday and intensify intermittently across several regions through Wednesday and Thursday.

According to the official weather bulletin issued on Sunday, October 25, 2026, conditions on Sunday feature fair skies with scattered clouds across the central region, and partly cloudy skies in the north and south with isolated chances of light showers.

Temperatures are expected to edge slightly higher across central and southern provinces while remaining near seasonal averages in the north, maintaining mild autumn conditions during daytime hours before turning cool overnight and early in the morning.

Monday will see fair to partly cloudy conditions nationwide, accompanied by light and variable winds and stable temperatures. By Tuesday, partly cloudy conditions will dominate across all provinces, with chances of light rain showers developing across western territories that could turn thundery at times, under light to moderate southeasterly winds.

Atmospheric instability will expand on Wednesday, bringing predominantly cloudy skies accompanied by light, occasionally thundery rain showers across western districts, before precipitation chances extend into northern and southern provinces.

Temperatures on Wednesday will rise slightly in the central and southern regions while dipping in the north.

Cloudy conditions and scattered rainfall ranging from light to moderate intensity—with occasional thundery activity—are projected to persist into Thursday.

The front will usher in a slight drop in temperatures across the central and northern governorates, while southern regions will see steady readings. Horizontal visibility will remain generally good, deteriorating temporarily during brief rain squalls or localized dust activity.

World.title: ‘Call of Duty’ North Korea invasion edition tops sales charts in South
World.content:
Seoul – The latest instalment of the “Call of Duty” video game franchise, featuring a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, has topped sales charts in the would-be target, even as real-life border tensions are ratcheting higher.

“Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4”, the latest edition of the globally popular franchise is set against a backdrop of tensions between the United States and Russia.

Its Friday release comes on the heels of an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean soldiers, further straining ties on the peninsula.

The game follows several parallel storylines: a squad of young American and South Korean soldiers fighting for survival, a former serviceman driven by revenge, and a power struggle surrounding a new North Korean leader — a character players can also take on.

The new edition has generated considerable interest in South Korea, where able-bodied men are required to serve between 18 and 21 months in the military, depending on the branch.

The title has topped both the global and South Korean sales charts on Steam, one of the world’s largest digital distribution platforms for PC games.

The campaign begins with a surprise invasion of South Korea by North Korean forces, who deploy paratroopers and infiltrate through an underground tunnel to catch South Korean and US troops off guard.

In reality, the US stations about 28,000 troops in South Korea to help deter the nuclear-armed North. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war because the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

Reactions among South Korean gamers have been largely positive, with some posting hashtags featuring a Korean slogan meaning “exterminate communism” on social media and others saying they were considering upgrading their computers or buying new consoles to play the title.

“I cried so much playing the game to a point I almost got dehydrated. It reminds me so much of my grandfather, who fought in the Korean War,” a Threads user with the handle b_yeol_t said.

Another user, posting under the handle ireozima_zebal, described the experience as “horrifying” because of its implications for a potential conflict on the Korean peninsula.

“This is what would unfold if the North launched an invasion, with the border province of Gangwon overwhelmed within an hour and our defence line pushed back right on the edge of Seoul,” the user said.

But the game has also drawn criticism for turning the fraught history between North and South Korea into entertainment.

The title raises the “question of whether it is appropriate… to present the tragedy of the Korean War and the current antagonism between South and North as something to be consumed for entertainment”, Kim Sung-jae, chairman of the Kim Dae Jung Peace Center, wrote in the Hankyoreh newspaper last month.

On Saturday, North Korean state media said leader Kim Jong Un had urged his military to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang last week.

World.title: ‘Tech debt coming due’: AI-found flaw signals chaos ahead
World.content:
Washington – Companies and government agencies rushed this week to patch two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs a large share of the world’s websites.

The vulnerability to potential hackers was found by using a powerful model from OpenAI in one of the most high-profile demonstration of AI’s cyber capabilities.

AFP spoke with Michael Daniel, president of the Cyber Threat Alliance and a former White House cybersecurity coordinator under former US president Barack Obama, about what the episode means as AI tools find software flaws faster than ever.

The interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Q: What does the PHP episode tell us?

A: This is the beginning of a pretty chaotic period, given the abilities of the advanced models. I’ve been saying for years that the logical conclusion of these AI models being able to find vulnerabilities at speed and at scale is that there’s going to be a flood of these vulnerabilities.

Rob Joyce [former cybersecurity director at the US National Security Agency] has referred to it as the great cleansing forest fire of old software. I’ve talked about our tech debt coming due.

The incentives have been for people to keep software as long as possible, and we don’t really factor these risks into the cost of having the software. You’re not incurring a direct cost on your books for this old software, but in reality you are, only it’s an implicit cost until something like this happens.

Q: What should organizations be doing?

A: Preparing to get your software updated, be prepared to keep it updated, and be prepared to implement patches when they come out.

There’s going to be a flood of vulnerabilities, a flood of patches and a flood of mitigations, and not all of them will be created equal.

For a lot of smaller organizations that don’t have a lot of internal capacity, what you’ve got to do is shift your organization to be able to accept the vendor updates as fast as you can.

Q: Is every flaw dangerous?

A: Historically, the exploitation rate for vulnerabilities has been five or six percent, and there’s no indication that number is going up. But now when bad guys exploit a vulnerability, they’re able to do so much more quickly.

It used to take a month or two for a proof of concept to come out, and then another month or two for it to show up in exploit kits (used by bad actors). That’s now measured in hours or days.

Q: What does that mean for large companies?

A: Most businesses essentially ran a zero-risk tolerance for breaking things, so they would test the hell out of a patch before they put it into production. Now they don’t have that time.

If the risk of breaking something by putting this patch into place is one percent, but the risk of being attacked could cost me 50 million dollars…now I’ve got an interesting trade-off.

Q: Are advanced AI tools reliable at finding real flaws?

A: There’s a lot of noise. The PHP one is a prime example of a real one, but there’s an awful lot out there that are either not real or are on software that’s never exposed to the internet. We’ve got to improve our triage system.

Q: Where does this lead us in two or three years?

A: We’re going to turn these AI tools on software that hasn’t been deployed yet, so one would hope we start to deploy software that has fewer vulnerabilities to begin with. You burn out all the old stuff, and it makes way for new growth that’s more secure from the beginning.

It’s not like this solves our cybersecurity problem, but it does change the nature of it going forward.

World.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady days ahead of US midterms
World.content:
Washington – The US Federal Reserve appears set to hold interest rates steady at its meeting next week, analysts say, despite stubbornly high inflation and with markets pricing in at least one rate hike before year-end.

The central bank’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet over two days, announcing its decision at 2:00 pm local time (18:00 GMT) on Wednesday.

The Fed has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, and at its last meeting in September the FOMC voted to raise the key federal funds rate for the first time in three years, lifting the target range to 3.75 percent to 4.0 percent.

The Fed’s meeting comes days ahead of key midterm elections in the United States on November 3, with the Democratic Party seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from US President Donald Trump’s Republicans.

Trump frequently berated and criticized Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s predecessor Jerome Powell over interest rates — which he deems to be too high — but has so far refrained from targeting the man he appointed to replace him over the issue.

The Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, hit a pandemic-era peak of 7.2 percent in 2022, before a series of interest-rate hikes tamed it to around 2.2 percent by late 2024.

Trump’s economic policies — including his upending of the global trade order using tariffs and his war on Iran — fuelled it once more, and it hit a three-year high of 3.9 percent in May.

Since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February, global energy prices have skyrocketed, with Tehran’s retaliatory actions sharply curtailing oil and gas supplies through the Gulf.

Higher energy prices have begun to cascade through into other goods and services, fuelling inflation in the United States, with prices a key issue for voters as they head to the polls.

– ‘Based on the economics’ –

Loretta Mester, former regional head of the Cleveland Fed, told AFP that the timing of the meeting just days ahead of the election would not be a factor for policymakers.

“The Fed doesn’t take into account any kind of political issues in that FOMC room,” she said. “It really is based on the economics.”

Mester argued that the fundamentals call for continuing to raise interest rates.

“The data that’s come in continue to show a stable labor market and continue to show inflation above target,” she said, adding that there was no evidence that it was on a path downwards towards the target.

“The economics would suggest then you need to continue raising rates.”

Still, she thought that most policymakers seemed keen to avoid moving too quickly, and may hold rates at this meeting, waiting to tighten the screws until the following meeting in early December.

Wendy Edelberg, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, believes central bankers would rather not put themselves in the middle of the political debate ahead of the midterms.

“It’s unhelpful for everyone if the Fed gets wrapped up in all the political discourse right before an election,” she told AFP.

Edelberg said that “there wouldn’t be huge economic implications” if policymakers raised rates in December as opposed to October.

She saw such a decision less as a “nod to Trump” — who has aggressively demanded lower rates to spur economic activity — and more a way to avoid being the potential target of political barbs.

Since returning to power last year, the US president has waged an unprecedented assault on the Fed’s independence, launching a criminal probe against Powell and attempting to unseat Fed Governor Lisa Cook.

The probe against Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh’s Senate confirmation, but the battle to fire Cook continues despite a Supreme Court decision nullifying an earlier attempt to do so.

Last week, Cook declined to attend a hearing in the White House’s probe into mortgage fraud allegations, which she denies.

World.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
World.content:
Washington – Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump’s Republican party.

The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party’s candidates.

In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.

“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown.

“Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”

“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”

Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate.

“Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year.

“You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.”

Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states.

“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said.

In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.

Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.

Obama also took digs at Trump’s renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the guilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure.

“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, referring to popular but indulgent American restaurant chain.

Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.

World.title: PM Modi inaugurates RBI's Rs 169-crore data centre, cybersecurity institute in Odisha
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

Spread across 18.55 acres, the facility's foundation stone was laid by then RBI governor Shaktikanta Das on March 22, 2023. The data centre will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other key RBI initiatives, according to a government statement.

It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services while providing a secure foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial sector.

The Cybersecurity Training Institute will focus on training, research and capacity building in cybersecurity and enterprise technology, helping strengthen capabilities across the financial sector.

The location was chosen for its geographical stability, away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, officials said according to news agency PTI. This is expected to reduce the facility's exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities.

World.title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
World.content:
The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujaratâs Kutch district.

According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. The fishermen were identified as Kadir Thaimor, Muhammad Mussa, Azgar Thaimor and Ahsan Jat, all residents of Chach Jaan Khan village in Pakistanâs Sindh province, according to information provided by the BSF.

Sir Creek is a narrow, marshy tidal channel in the Rann of Kutch, along the coastal region between Gujarat and Pakistanâs Sindh province.

The area is strategically sensitive because the longstanding India-Pakistan boundary dispute over the creek affects the demarcation of the maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea.

The regionâs shallow waters, tidal channels and extensive marshlands make navigation and border surveillance challenging. Fishing activities in the area can also lead to fishermen crossing into the other countryâs waters, prompting apprehensions by security personnel.

World.title: 'Too deferential to govt': Former SC judge questions ex-CJI Chandrachud’s approach to appointments
World.content:
Congress flags judicial independence concerns over claims in ex SC judge's memoir

Congress flags judicial independence concerns

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Is Justice D Y Chandrachud's approach to judicial appointments acceptable in your opinion? Yes, he is doing what's necessary. No, it undermines judicial independence. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has questioned former Chief Justice of India (CJI) D Y Chandrachud's approach to judicial appointments, alleging that he was "too deferential to the government". He also expressed concern over the practice of discussing candidates with the executive before formal Collegium deliberations.In his forthcoming memoir, Without Fear or Favour, Justice Kaul recounts a Collegium meeting to fill six vacancies in the Supreme Court, during which five names had been agreed upon in advance. He alleges that Justice Chandrachud proposed a sixth candidate at the last minute and considered seeking the government's view on the appointment."The Chief Justice drew me aside into a separate room and wondered aloud whether he should telephone out to check the government's view," Kaul wrote in his book.Speaking to news portal The Wire about his memoir, Kaul said the Collegium must resist executive pressure to safeguard judicial independence.Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was trying to please the government or seeking its prior approval, Kaul said, "I don't think it was a question of pleasing the government, but what had happened was that he had discussed the names with me earlier."We had agreed on five names, and I thought the collegium would be quite okay with the other members of the collegium, and this (sixth) name was propped up at the last minute with me while going to the collegium meeting. I said that name is not acceptable to me and will not be acceptable."He said Justice Chandrachud wanted him to support the additional candidate, but he believed the other Collegium members would also oppose the proposal."And well, he wanted me to collaborate and go ahead with the name. I said even if I do that, the others will not. I believe, and that's what happened in the meeting. I told him this will not get through because I know the views of the other collegiate members. Maybe he had already taken some kind of an approval for the other names, including the sixth name," Kaul said.He expressed concern over the practice of discussing judicial appointments with the government before formal Collegium meetings."So this has become, unfortunately, a practice of names being discussed in some kind of a previous discussion with the government," he told senior journalist Karan Thapar."It has been happening, I think, before and after, which is what troubles me. That's why I have written that when the government introduced the NJAC (the National Judicial Appointments Commission) in 2015, we would at least have sat across the table and discussed it. It could have been fine-tuned. It could be modulated," Kaul said.Justice Kaul, who retired in December 2023, wrote that differences over how to deal with the executive strained his relationship with Justice Chandrachud, under whom he served on the Collegium from June 2022."There is a difference between consultation and what I came to regard as pre-approval, seeking the government's nod before the collegium had even formally deliberated," Kaul wrote in his memoir.Explaining why he considered Justice Chandrachud "too deferential to the government on appointment matters," Kaul said the practice could create difficulties for future Chief Justices, particularly those with shorter tenures."Well, he believed that this is how it had been happening, and I was of the view that you, with a chief justice like you, and with two years' tenure, and with your own merit and the trust, if you do this, the successors would have a problem in not following this practice because they have shorter tenures.""And the government would get used to a particular methodology before appointments to the Supreme Court were made, and that's why I endeavoured to discourage him from discussing everything beforehand," Kaul said.The former judge also raised objections to the transfer of a case concerning the reconsideration of certain aspects of a Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) judgment from a bench headed by him to another bench. He argued that cases should not be reassigned because of apprehensions about how a particular bench might decide them.The Congress on Sunday raised concerns over the independence of the judiciary under the Narendra Modi government, citing revelations in the forthcoming memoir. The party asserted that the institution responsible for upholding the Constitution must remain free from pressure exerted by those in power.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report quoting the pre-publication manuscript of Kaul's memoir, Without Fear of Favour, which reportedly states that Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice D Y Chandrachud was "too deferential to the Government" on judicial appointments.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "A book by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has raised serious questions regarding the independence of the judiciary during the tenure of the Modi government."Ramesh said Kaul had highlighted several concerning incidents, including alleged government interference in judicial appointments, attempts to secure government approval before Collegium meetings and the government's questioning of the caste of a judge belonging to a minority community.He added that issues many had previously been hesitant to discuss openly had now been documented by Kaul in measured and deliberate language."Strikingly, a former Chief Justice of India (CJI) has not denied that discussions with the government take place prior to judicial appointments. When former CJI Justice Chandrachud acknowledges that the government engages with the CJI and plays a role in the appointment process, the concerns surrounding judicial independence become even more profound," Ramesh said.The Congress leader also flagged Kaul's account of an incident involving a case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). According to Ramesh, Kaul revealed that after a bench presided over by him raised the possibility of reconsidering certain aspects of a court ruling in the case, the matter was reassigned to another bench without consulting him."This points to the extent of the government's day-to-day interference in the functioning of the Supreme Court," Ramesh said.Questioning the implications of the alleged incidents, he said, "When there is pressure to obtain government approval for judicial appointments, and when benches hearing sensitive cases are altered, one must ask -- in the interest of safeguarding democracy -- if this does not constitute pressure on the judiciary and an erosion of its independence, then what does?"Emphasising the importance of judicial independence in a democracy, Ramesh said, "The institution tasked with upholding the Constitution must remain free from the pressures of those in power. In a democracy, the independence of the judiciary is not merely an option; it is an absolute necessity," Ramesh asserted.

World.title: 'Second war of independence': Kharge targets BJP-RSS, calls for nationwide movement against SIR

NEW DELHI: Congress president

Addressing a gathering in Patna, Kharge said, "As long as RSS ideology is not eliminated, there will be no peace in the country." He also expressed disappointment over Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's alliance with those who follow the RSS ideology.

"I am pained that socialist leaders like Nitish Kumar joined hands with people who believe in RSS ideology," Kharge said.

Calling the ongoing political struggle a "second war of independence", Kharge urged the people of Bihar to support a nationwide movement against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

"This is second war of independence; I urge the people of Bihar to support nationwide movement against SIR," he said.

Kharge alleged that governments had been formed through 'vote chori' in West Bengal, Haryana, Bihar and Maharashtra, and warned that those responsible would face legal consequences.

"Govts stolen through 'vote chori' in Bengal, Haryana, Bihar, Maharashtra; these thieves will be put behind bars," he said.





The Congress president also called for action against those involved in the alleged 'suddhikaran' (purification) targeting him. He said BJP leader J P Nadda had promised an inquiry into the incident, but an FIR was instead filed against Rahul Gandhi when he visited Haldwani.

"We need to find those involved in carrying out 'suddhikaran' (purification)," Kharge said.

He also targeted the BJP over the Ayodhya temple row, saying, "I pray to Lord Ram to open his eyes, punish those who have looted wealth in his name."

Kharge further accused the BJP and RSS of undoing the legacy of Bihar's prominent leaders, including Rajendra Prasad.

Taking aim at the government's handling of inflation, Kharge questioned its promise of ushering in 'Amrit Kaal' while essential food items remained unaffordable.

"This govt, which cannot make onions and bread affordable, how will it usher in 'Amrit Kaal'," he asked.

The Congress president also demanded that all elections be conducted using ballot papers, the SIR exercise be halted immediately and Assembly elections held over the past two years be annulled.

Meanwhile, in a communication to party MPs, Kharge asked them to remain present in Delhi on October 30, 31 and November 1, 2026, in connection with the ongoing protests by INDIA bloc parties over alleged electoral irregularities and 'vote chori'.

The communication cited allegations of irregularities by the ECI and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) as the reasons for the directive. It also referred to the planned 'Save the Vote, Save the Country Jan March and Mega Rally', scheduled to be held at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on November 1.

Earlier on Sunday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urged students, farmers, labourers, women, youth and traders to participate in the rally, alleging that names had been deleted from voter lists and electoral rules and laws had been violated.

World.title: Firefighters rescue nine persons trapped in the middle of Vellar in Perambalur district
World.content:
In a swift operation, a team of firefighters rescued nine persons who got trapped in the sudden rise in water level in the Vellar near Labbaikudikadu in Perambalur district after heavy rain in the catchment areas on Sunday. The rescue operation lasted nearly two hours soon after the crack of dawn when the firefighters armed with necessary paraphernalia managed to rescue the nine persons one after the other using manila ropes and life buoys.

The fire station at Veppur in Perambalur district received information around 5 a.m. about a group of people trapped in the middle of the Vellar after sudden rise in water flow. A team from the Veppur fire station rushed to the spot within 10 minutes armed with equipment used for the rescue operation.

Another team from the Perambalur fire station headed by the Assistant District Fire Officer reached the spot to augment manpower, a Fire Department official told The Hindu. About 15 firefighters, along with a few volunteers, were involved in the rescue mission. The rescue team positioned itself on a new bridge was under construction across the Vellar.

The firefighters noticed a group of nine men standing atop a sports utility vehicle, a few metres away from the bridge under construction. The vehicle was partially submerged in the water.

The vehicle was stuck in the middle due to sudden surge in water level, an official said. The firefighting team threw manila ropes tying life buoys with it and rope ladder towards the group. The group members caught hold of the nylon rope and the firefighters pulled them to safety one after the other.

World.title: Kalpathy delegation visits Tamil Nadu temples ahead of chariot fest
World.content:
Representatives of four Kalpathy temples visited Mayuranathaswamy Temple at Mayiladuthurai in Tamil Nadu on Sunday to honour their historical links ahead of the Kalpathy chariot festival to be held from November 7 to 17. The delegation offered prayers and presented festival invitations to the temple. It also visited temples at Vaitheeswaran Koil, Thiruvarur, Thiruvidaimarudur and Kumbakonam, and met Swami Vimuktananda, head of the Sri Ramakrishna Math in Thanjavur.

The Mayiladuthurai temple’s chariot festival is believed to have inspired the Kalpathy car festival. Tamil Brahmins who settled in Palakkad in the 13th century are believed to have come from Mayiladuthurai, Kumbakonam and Thanjavur, bringing their Vedic scholarship and temple traditions. “The festival would be incomplete without remembering our ancestors. We visited these temples to honour our forebears and seek their blessings,” said K.S. Krishna, convener of the Kalpathy festival committee.

The Kalpathy car festival follows a tradition similar to the chariot festival held during the last 10 days of the Tamil month of Aippasi in Mayiladuthurai. The festival has been celebrated in Kalpathy for centuries.

The four participating temples are Sri Visalakshi Sametha Sri Viswanathaswamy Temple at Kalpathy, Mandakkara Sri Mahaganapathy Temple at New Kalpathy, Sri Lakshminarayana Perumal Temple at Old Kalpathy and Sri Prasanna Mahaganapathy Temple at Chathapuram.

The delegation, led by temple committee office-bearers C.V. Murali Ramanathan, K.S. Krishna and A.V. Vasudevan, included representatives and residents of the four Kalpathy agraharams. It invited priests, religious leaders and devotees in Tamil Nadu to attend the temple car festival.

World.title: Keralam government hikes compensations for human-wildlife conflict victims by 25%
World.content:
The Keralam government has increased compensation and medical assistance for victims of human-wildlife conflict by 25%. The maximum compensation for deaths caused by wildlife attacks has been increased to ₹17.5 lakh.

The revised compensation rates provide enhanced financial assistance to the dependants of those killed in wildlife attacks, persons who suffer permanent disabilities, and those injured in such incidents. The revision was introduced as part of the State government’s 100-day action programme.

Under the revised rates, the compensation for deaths caused by wildlife attacks, except those involving elephants, wild boars and bee attacks, has been raised from ₹14 lakh to ₹17.5 lakh. For deaths resulting from attacks by elephants, wild boars and bees, the solatium has been revised from ₹4 lakh to ₹5 lakh.

The government has also enhanced compensation rates for victims who suffer permanent disabilities. The assistance for persons who suffer disabilities ranging from 40% to 60%, including the loss of a limb or eye, has been raised from ₹2 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh.

For those sustaining permanent disability over 60%, the compensation has been raised from ₹2.5 lakh to ₹3.125 lakh. In addition, a financial grant of up to ₹1 lakh can also be sanctioned from the Chief Minister’s Distress Relief Fund (CMDRF).

Rare and severe cases

In rare and severe cases that require prolonged care where expenses exceed ₹2.25 lakh, the actual costs can be sanctioned directly from the CMDRF based on the treating doctor’s certificate without needing a separate government order.

The order also streamlines treatment assistance for persons hospitalised with severe injuries. For victims requiring hospitalisation for more than a week, the assistance that was previously capped between ₹16,000 and ₹1 lakh has been hiked to a maximum ceiling of ₹1.25 lakh. For victims hospitalised for less than a week, assistance ranging from ₹5,400 to ₹1 lakh will continue under standard provisions without requiring CMDRF allocation.

World.title: Naidu puts officials on high alert as cyclone nears Andhra Pradesh coast
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Sunday reviewed the State’s preparedness to deal with the impending cyclone, directing officials to remain on high alert and minimise disruption to people’s lives.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm and subsequently a severe cyclonic storm, according to the forecast presented at the review meeting. Ten National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams have been kept ready for relief and rescue operations.

Officials briefed the Chief Minister on evacuation plans, rehabilitation centres, food and drinking water supplies, medical assistance, power restoration and other precautionary measures.

The cyclone is likely to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam between the morning and afternoon of October 28. Current projections indicate a possible landfall along the Konaseema-Yanam-Kakinada coastal belt.

The system is currently located about 850 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 930 km from Kakinada. It is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26, a severe cyclonic storm by that night and a very severe cyclonic storm on October 27.

Wind speeds at landfall could reach 115-125 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph in some areas. Coastal districts are likely to experience strong winds from the morning of October 27.

Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast in North Andhra and the central coastal districts on October 27 and 28, with isolated places likely to receive exceptionally heavy rainfall.

Kakinada, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Konaseema and East Godavari districts, along with other parts of North Andhra, are likely to be affected by strong winds and heavy rain.

According to projections presented at the meeting, Anakapalli district could receive an average rainfall of 292.55 mm, followed by Alluri Sitarama Raju district at 281.17 mm, Visakhapatnam at 253.87 mm and Srikakulam at 249.18 mm. The State’s average cumulative rainfall over five days is estimated at 95 mm, while the average rainfall in the affected districts could range from 22 cm to 29 cm.

Mr. Naidu instructed officials to coordinate across departments and make advance arrangements to minimise the impact on residents. He stressed the need for continuous monitoring, a high level of preparedness and advance planning.

He directed officials to ensure that all boats operating at sea returned to the coast and advised fishermen against venturing into the sea as conditions were expected to become extremely rough.

The Chief Minister also asked officials to take all necessary steps to utilise the expected flood inflows to replenish reservoirs.

Chief Secretary Sai Prasad, DGP Harish Gupta, district collectors and officials from the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and the Agriculture, Power, Irrigation, Home, Health, Civil Supplies, Municipal Administration and Panchayat Raj departments attended the meeting.
